Note:’NST’ means No Notified Scheduled Tribes

The latest census-based figures of ST population will be available after the release of the next population census.

The Government continues to support the welfare and socio-economic development of Scheduled Tribes through various schemes and interventions of the Ministry of Tribal Affairs. These include Dharti Aaba Janjatiya Gram Utkarsh Abhiyan (DAJGUA) for saturation of infrastructure and basic services in tribal villages; Pradhan Mantri Janjati Adivasi Nyaya Maha Abhiyan (PM JANMAN) for the holistic development of Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Groups (PVTGs); Eklavya Model Residential Schools (EMRS) for providing quality residential education to tribal students; Pre-Matric, Post-Matric, National Scholarship for Higher Education, National Fellowship and National Overseas Scholarship Schemes for educational support; Grants under Article 275(1) of the Constitution for bridging critical infrastructure gaps in Scheduled Areas and tribal areas; Grant-in-Aid to Voluntary Organisations for education, health and livelihood initiatives; Pradhan Mantri Janjatiya Vikas Mission (PMJVM), National Scheduled Tribes Finance and Development Corporation (NSTFDC) and Venture Capital Fund for Scheduled Tribes (VCF-ST) for promoting sustainable livelihoods, entrepreneurship and concessional credit; and Tribal Research, Information, Education, Communication and Events (TRI-ECE) for research, documentation and capacity building. In addition, health, education, drinking water, connectivity and other infrastructure-related interventions are being implemented through convergence with the concerned Ministries/Departments.

As per available information no proposal for grant of Scheduled Tribe status to any community on the basis of duration of residence in the UT of Delhi is under consideration in this Ministry. Grant of Scheduled Tribe status is governed by Article 342 of the Constitution, under which a community can be specified as a Scheduled Tribe only through a notification issued by the President after consultation with the Governor/Administrator concerned, and any subsequent inclusion or exclusion is affected only by an Act of Parliament amending the Constitution (Scheduled Tribes) Order, 1950. Such proposals are examined against the criteria recommended by the Lokur Committee (1965) — namely, indications of primitive traits, distinctive culture, geographical isolation, shyness of contact with the community at large, and social and economic backwardness — and require a specific recommendation from the concerned State Government/UT Administration, followed by concurrence of the Registrar General of India and the National Commission for Scheduled Tribes.

Reservation for Scheduled Tribes in Union Territories is presently provided as under:

(i) Political institutions: Reservation of seats for STs in the UT Legislative Assemblies/Panchayats/Municipalities is provided in proportion to their population under the respective Government of Union Territories Act, 1963, the Delimitation Act, 2002 and other applicable local laws, in Union Territories having notified ST population, namely Lakshadweep, Andaman & Nicobar Islands, and Dadra & Nagar Haveli and Daman & Diu. No such reservation applies in Chandigarh, Delhi and Puducherry, since no ST is notified therein.

(ii) Administrative services: Reservation in direct recruitment to civil posts and services under the Union Territory administrations follows the reservation policy of the Department of Personnel & Training (DoPT), Government of India, which prescribes 7.5% reservation for Scheduled Tribes at the all-India level. In Union Territories with a predominant or substantial ST population (such as Lakshadweep and Dadra & Nagar Haveli), a higher percentage of reservation is provided in local/UT cadre recruitment, commensurate with the local ST population, as notified by the respective UT Administration from time to time.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Tribal Affairs
STATUS OF EMRSs
Posted On: 30 JUL 2026 1:44PM by PIB Delhi

Replying to a question in Lok Sabha today the Union Minister of State for Tribal Affairs Shri Durgadas Uikey informed that as on date, 728 Eklavya Model Residential Schools (EMRSs) are approved across the country out of which 508 are functional. In Bihar, 03 EMRSs have been approved, of which 02 EMRSs are functional. The inauguration of 43 new EMRSs during 2025-26 is an effort to expand the EMRS network in the country.

 Various steps have been undertaken to enhance the quality of education and sports facilities in EMRSs across the country which are well-equipped classrooms with modern teaching aids, bridge courses, remedial classes science and computer laboratories, libraries with diverse learning resources, playgrounds and sports equipment, facilities for extracurricular activities like music, art, and sports, smart classrooms for digital education, computer labs with internet access, skill development and vocational training programs on apparel, Automotive, AR/VR, AI, Beauty & Wellness, Agriculture, Electronics, and retail to enhance employability, etc.

 To address the issue of vacancies, 9111 teaching & non -teaching staff have already been recruited and examination has been conducted for another batch of 7267 teaching & non -teaching staff for EMRSs across the country. In addition, State Governments have also been advised to depute staff on deputation and contract basis to address the issue of vacancies so that academic activities are not hampered.

In order to bridge the infrastructure gap in EMRSs, several measures have been taken such as Standardised designs ensuring modern academic facilities, hostels, staff quarters, and sports infrastructure; additional grants for upgradation of old schools; regular monitoring through third-party inspections etc.

Further, National Education Society for Tribal Students (NESTS) continuously follows up with the State Governments and the execution agencies to fast-track construction of EMRSs and to make them functional at the earliest. Besides, State Governments have also been advised to make the EMRS functional in alternative buildings, wherever feasible.

 The expansion of EMRSs aligns with the Government's objectives of inclusive education and empowerment of tribal communities in the following manner:

  • EMRSs provide access to quality residential education to Scheduled Tribe (ST) students in remote and tribal-dominated areas, thereby reducing educational disparities.
  • The scheme promotes equitable access to educational opportunities by providing free education along with boarding and lodging facilities.
  • EMRSs focus on the holistic development of tribal students through academic excellence, sports, skill development, and extracurricular activities.
  • The scheme enhances educational attainment, employability and leadership potential among tribal youth, contributing to their socio-economic empowerment.
  • The expansion of EMRSs supports the Government's commitment to inclusive and accessible education for tribal communities across the country.

Ministry of Tribal Affairs
Implementation of DAJGUA
Posted On: 30 JUL 2026 1:44PM by PIB Delhi

Replying to a question in Lok Sabha today the Union Minister of State for Tribal Affairs Shri Durgadas Uikey informed that the number of tribal beneficiaries eligible to receive benefits under the Dharti Aaba Janjatiya Gram Utkarsh Abhiyan (DAJGUA) across various States and Union Territories is at Annexure I.

Under Dharti Aaba Janjatiya Gram Utkarsh Abhiyan (DAJGUA), the Ministry of Tribal Affairs have regular Inter – Ministerial and coordination meetings with line ministries under DAJGUA, to ensure effective implementation of the scheme. Further, regular review meetings are also held with respective States/ Districts Authority. Provision of PMU has also been made for effective monitoring and implementation of the scheme. Furthermore, through the initiatives Adi KarmaYogi Abhiyan, the Ministry has been actively encouraging community engagement and involvement also. The Monitoring and Evaluation Framework under the Dharti Aaba Janjatiya Gram Utkarsh Abhiyan also provides for a technology-enabled monitoring system through the PM GatiShakti Portal to track progress in real time.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Tribal Affairs
IMPLEMENTATION OF PM-JANMAN IN KERALA
Posted On: 30 JUL 2026 1:43PM by PIB Delhi

Replying to a question in Lok Sabha today the Union Minister of State for Tribal Affairs Shri Durgadas Uikey informed that the Ministry has been monitoring the implementation of the interventions under Pradhan Mantri Janjati Adivasi Nyaya Maha AbhiyaN (PMJANMAN) across the implementing states including State of Kerala. The assessment of progress is undertaken through periodic reviews, field-level monitoring, and reports received from the concerned State Government and implementing agencies. The progress so made under the abhiyan has contributed to the socio-economic development of PVTGs in the State of Kerala through improvement in basic amenities and livelihood opportunities. The details of the benefits given under PM JANMAN, as on 30.06.2026, Ministry-wise, in Kerala, are given at Annexure I.

No specific representation has been received or challenge has been noticed in implementation of PM JANMAN in Kerala.

The Ministry is regularly coordinating with concerned line Ministries/Departments and the State Tribal Welfare Department / other line State Departments for implementation of the existing interventions under the PM JANMAN and to expedite the achievements of the targets. Further, to ensure the effective implementation of the PM JANMAN, the Ministry has established a Project Monitoring Unit at the national level. This unit regularly coordinates with line Ministries and State Governments to assess progress.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Steel
Financial discipline and operational foresight drive SAIL’s Q1 FY27 profit surge
Posted On: 30 JUL 2026 1:42PM by PIB Delhi

SAIL’s Q1 FY27 performance is not just about a sharp rise in profits y-o-y, it is about how financial acumen and operational foresight came together to deliver results. Commenting on SAIL’s performance in the first quarter of the FY27, Chairman & Managing Director, Dr. Ashok Kumar Panda said, “This performance reflects the strength of SAIL’s integrated strategy. Even as the global headwinds generated due to volatility in the Middle East posed challenges, we demonstrated resilience through financial prudence combined with proactive operational measures. The performance during the quarter reflected a conscious drive towards efficiency improvement. Equally important was the company’s disciplined approach to cash flow management, strict financial controls and sharper working capital practices.”

Going into the details on the prudent financial management strategy adopted by SAIL, he added that, “During the first quarter, the company contained borrowings and reduced the cost of borrowings through long standing financial credibility and further improvement in management of cash flows and debt. Liquidity remained strong, and both the debt–equity ratio and net debt–EBITDA profile showed marked improvement, highlighting SAIL’s success in reducing debt exposure while sustaining profitability.”

Q1 FY27 reflected progress in company’s product mix and investment priorities. The proportion of finished steel in the total saleable steel improved to 89% in Q1 FY27 from 86% over CPLY, indicating a gradual reduction of semis in the company’s overall product basket. The percentage of value‑added steel dispatches also increased by 7.5% in Q1 FY27 over CPLY, reinforcing SAIL’s focus on quality‑driven growth. At the same time, CAPEX exceeded the target from ₹2,306 Crore to ₹2,575 Crore, highlighting the company’s strong commitment to strategic investments and proactive allocation of resources towards capacity expansion and modernization.

The quarter also showcased SAIL’s ability to translate strategy into operational resilience. Blast furnace productivity improved, steelmaking economics were reinforced through optimized ferro‑alloys and flux consumption, and scheduled capital repairs were advanced proactively to secure stability for the coming quarters. Dr. Panda further elaborated that “Our focus on operational foresight ensured uninterrupted performance despite supply chain disruptions. While limestone requirements were met through a balanced mix of indigenous and external sources, alternate arrangements for Propane gas safeguarded continuity.”

The focused thrust on mining operations delivered significant results by unlocking the full potential of SAIL's captive mines. Enhanced iron ore production enabled the Company to fully meet its internal raw material requirements while marketing surplus ore in the domestic market. As a result, iron ore sales during Q1FY27 registered an impressive 269% growth over the corresponding period of the previous year. This exceptional performance provided a significant boost to the Company's bottom line and underscored the strategic strength of SAIL's integrated business model, wherein value creation across the mining and steel value chain directly translates into superior operational and financial performance.

Taken together, these developments underscore how SAIL is not only delivering financial resilience but also reshaping its product portfolio and investing in future‑ready infrastructure - laying the foundation for sustained competitiveness in a volatile global environment.

****

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Steel
MOIL Reports Strong Performance in Q1 FY 2026-27; Profit After Tax Up by 70%
Posted On: 30 JUL 2026 1:41PM by PIB Delhi

The Board of Directors of MOIL Limited approved the financial and operational results for the first quarter of FY 2026-27 (Q1 FY27). The company recorded steady growth across production, sales volume, and overall profitability.

Financial Highlights (Q1 FY 2026-27 vs Q1 FY 2025-26):

  • Revenue from Operations: Increased by 7% to ₹370.88 crore, up from ₹348.06 crore.
  • Total Revenue: Rose by 6% to ₹391.13 crore compared to ₹370.52 crore.
  • Profit Before Tax (PBT): Registered a 75% increase to ₹111.62 crore from ₹63.82 crore.
  • Profit After Tax (PAT): Increased by 70% to ₹87.62 crore compared to ₹51.51 crore.
  • Net Sales Realization (NSR): Reached ₹9,749 per MT, reflecting a 10% gain over ₹8,884 per MT in the corresponding previous quarter.

Operational Highlights:

  • Manganese Ore Production: Stood at 507,605 MT, marking a 1% increase over 502,260 MT recorded in Q1 FY26.
  • Manganese Ore Sales: Reached 369,049 MT, up by 4% from 356,196 MT in the same period last year.

Appreciating the efforts of the team, MOIL management said, "These results reflect the dedication and hard work of our entire workforce. The operational discipline and commitment shown by our team have enabled the company to maintain growth across key metrics. As we move forward, MOIL remains focused on achieving higher production targets, improving operational efficiency, and meeting the growing requirements of the domestic steel industry."

MOIL Limited is a Schedule ‘A’ Miniratna Category-I Central Public Sector Enterprise under the Ministry of Steel, Government of India. It is the largest producer of manganese ore in the country, operating underground and open-cast mines across Maharashtra and Madhya Pradesh.

*****

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Tribal Affairs
Scheduled Tribes in Kerala
Posted On: 30 JUL 2026 1:40PM by PIB Delhi

Replying to a question in Lok Sabha today the Union Minister of State for Tribal Affairs Shri Durgadas Uikey informed that as per Census 2011, the Scheduled Tribe (ST) population of Kerala is 4,84,839, constituting 1.45 per cent of the total population of the State. The districts having the highest Scheduled Tribe population are Wayanad, Idukki, Palakkad, Kasaragod and Kannur.

The Scheduled Tribes and Other Traditional Forest Dwellers (Recognition of Forest Rights) Act, 2006 is implemented by the respective State Governments and Union Territory Administrations, while the Ministry of Tribal Affairs monitors its implementation through Monthly Progress Reports received from them. As per MPR of MoTA, 2,923 Individual Forest Rights (IFR) titles and 110 Community Forest Rights (CFR) titles, aggregating 3033 forest rights titles, have been distributed under the Act.

The Government accords high priority to the socio-economic development of Scheduled Tribes, including those residing in Kerala. Issues relating to land rights, education, health, nutrition and livelihood are addressed through implementation of the Forest Rights Act, 2006 and various schemes of the Central and State Governments. Matters relating to land alienation are dealt with by the State Government under the applicable State laws, while health and nutrition interventions are implemented through convergence under various Central and State Government programmes.

The government continues to support the welfare and development of Scheduled tribes in Kerala through various interventions:

  1. Dharti Aaba Janjatiya Gram Utkarsh Abhiyan: Hon'ble PM launched Dharti Aaba Janjatiya Gram Utkarsh Abhiyan Hon'ble PM launched Dharti Aaba Janjatiya Gram Utkarsh Abhiyan (DAJGUA) on 2nd October, 2024. The Abhiyan comprises of 25 interventions implemented by 17-line Ministries and aims to saturate infrastructural gaps in 63,843 villages, provide social infrastructure like hostels, Anganwadi facilities and mobile medical units and set up Van Dhan Vikas Kendras to provide livelihood opportunities benefiting more than 5 crore tribals in 549 districts and 2,911 blocks in 30 States/UTs in 5 years. The Abhiyan has a total budgetary outlay of Rs.79,156 Cr (Central share: ₹56,333 Cr and State share: ₹22,823 Cr)
  2. Pre-Matric Scholarships to ST students: The scheme is applicable to students who are studying in Classes IX –X. Parental income from all sources should not be more than Rs.2.50 lakhs per annum. Scholarship of Rs.225/-per month for day scholars and Rs.525/-per month for hostellers is given for a period of 10 months in a year. Scholarship is disbursed through the State Government/UT Administration. Funding ratio is 75:25 between Centre and States for all States except North East and Hills States/UT like Himachal Pradesh, Uttarakhand and Jammu and Kashmir where it is 90:10.For UTs without legislature sharing pattern is 100% Central share.
  3. Post Matric Scholarship to ST students: The objective of the scheme is to provide financial assistance to the Scheduled Tribe students studying at post-matriculation or post-secondary levels to enable them to complete their education. Parental income from all sources should not be more than Rs.2.50 lakhs per annum. Compulsory fees charged by educational institutions are reimbursed subject to the limit fixed by the concerned State Fee fixation committee and scholarship amount of Rs.230 to Rs.1200 per month, depending upon the course of study is paid. The Scheme is implemented by the State Governments and Union Territory Administrations. Funding ratio is 75:25 between Centre and States for all States except NE and Hilly States/UT of Himachal Pradesh, Uttarakhand and Jammu and Kashmir where it is 90:10. For UTs without legislature sharing pattern is 100% Central share.
  4. National Scholarship Scheme for Higher Education of ST Students (earlier known as Top Class Scholarship Scheme): Under this Scheme, Scholarship is provided for pursuing Graduate/Post Graduate courses in the selected top-class Government and Non-Government Institutes in professional fields such as Management, Medicine, Engineering, Information Technology, Law etc. All the ST students, with annual parental income is not exceeding Rs.6.0 lakhs and studying in the 265 notified institutes by the Ministry, are eligible to receive scholarship. This scheme is started from year 2007-08 (b) National Fellowship Scheme for Higher Education of ST Students: It is a Central Sector Scheme, fully funded by Ministry of Tribal Aﬀairs to grant scholarship to meritorious ST students for pursuing Ph.D in India after completion of Master degree. This scheme is started from year 2005-06. The total number of fresh fellowships for Ph.D every year will be 750. ST students with a minimum of 55% marks in Master Degree up to the age of 36 years are eligible to apply for fellowship under the Scheme. The value of fellowship is at par with UGC rates.
  5. National Overseas Scholarship for ST students: It is a Central Sector Scheme of Ministry of Tribal Aﬀairs under which scholarships are given to the meritorious Schedule Tribe (ST) students for pursuing higher education in top 1000 ranked (as per latest QS world ranking) Institutes/Universities abroad. This scheme is started from year 1954-55. The Scheme is implemented through the Indian Embassies/Missions abroad, Ministry of External Aﬀairs. Twenty awards are given every year. ST students with annual family income not exceeding Rs.6.0 lakhs are eligible to apply for the Scholarship under the Scheme.
  6. Pradhan Mantri Janjati Adivasi Nyaya Maha Abhiyan (PM JANMAN): Government launched Pradhan Mantri Janjati Adivasi Nyaya Maha Abhiyan (PM JANMAN) for socio-economic development of 75 PVTG communities residing in 18 states and one UT. The mission aims to provide basic facilities such as safe housing, clean drinking water and improved access to education, health and nutrition, road and telecom connectivity, electrification of unelectrified households and sustainable livelihood opportunities in 3 years. These objectives are planned to be met through 11 interventions including Hostels and Mobile Medical Units (MMUs) implemented by 9-line Ministries. PM JANMAN has total budgetary outlay of Rs.24,104 Cr (Central share: ₹15336 Cr and State share: ₹8768 Cr).
  7. Grants under Article 275(1) of the Constitution: Under the Proviso to Article 275(1) of Constitution, Grants are released to States, having ST population for raising the level of administration in Scheduled Areas and for the welfare of tribal people. This is a Special Area Programme and 100% grants are provided to States. Funds are released to the State Governments depending on the felt needs of ST population to bridge the gap in infrastructure activities in the fields of education, health, skill development, livelihood, drinking water, sanitation, etc.
  8. Grant-in Aid to Voluntary Organizations working for the welfare of Scheduled Tribes: Under the scheme of Grant-in-Aid to Voluntary Organizations working for the welfare of Scheduled Tribes, the Ministry funds projects in the fields of education and health, covering residential schools, non-residential schools, hostels, mobile dispensaries, ten or more bedded hospitals, livelihood, etc.
  9. Eklavya Model Residential Schools (EMRS): The Scheme provides quality residential education to Scheduled Tribe students in remote and tribal areas with the objective of enabling them to access quality education comparable to the best institutions in the country. The schools provide modern educational infrastructure along with facilities for holistic development of tribal students.
  10. Pradhan Mantri Janjatiya Vikas Mission (PMJVM): The Mission promotes sustainable livelihoods of Scheduled Tribes through value addition, entrepreneurship development, marketing support and strengthening of tribal producer organisations, with emphasis on value chains based on Minor Forest Produce and other tribal products.
  11. Tribal Research, Information, Education, Communication and Events (TRI-ECE): The Scheme supports Tribal Research Institutes for research, documentation, capacity building, preservation and promotion of tribal culture, awareness generation, information dissemination and evidence-based policy support.
  12. National Scheduled Tribes Finance and Development Corporation (NSTFDC): under the Ministry of Tribal Affairs is an apex organisation set up exclusively for economic development of Scheduled Tribes implements various schemes for livelihood generation. NSTFDC extends concessional loans to the eligible Scheduled Tribe communities.
  13. Venture Capital Fund for Scheduled Tribes (VCF-ST): The Scheme is implemented through the National Scheduled Tribes Finance and Development Corporation (NSTFDC) to provide concessional venture capital assistance to Scheduled Tribe entrepreneurs for establishment and expansion of income-generating enterprises.
  14. Strengthening of health, education, drinking water, connectivity and other infrastructure through convergence with Ministries/Departments and the Government of Kerala.

RN

(Release ID: 2291612)

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Tribal Affairs
STRENGTHENING AND EXPANSION OF EMRSs
Posted On: 30 JUL 2026 1:39PM by PIB Delhi

Replying to a question in Lok Sabha today the Union Minister of State for Tribal Affairs Shri Durgadas Uikey informed that Ministry of Tribal Affairs is implementing the scheme of Eklavya Model Residential School (EMRS) for providing quality education to tribal students in their own environment preserving local art and culture. EMRS are established in tribal dominated blocks having more than 50% ST population and at least 20,000 tribal persons, as per Census 2011. As on date, 728 EMRSs have been approved out of which 508 are functional across the country.

Various steps have been undertaken to enhance the quality of education and extra-curricular activities in EMRSs across the country viz. well-equipped classrooms with modern teaching aids, bridge courses, remedial classes science and computer laboratories, libraries with diverse learning resources, playgrounds and sports equipment, facilities for extracurricular activities like music, art, and sports, smart classrooms for digital education, computer labs with internet access, skill development and vocational training programs on apparel, Automotive, AR/VR, AI, Beauty & Wellness, Agriculture, Electronics, and retail to enhance employability, etc.

To strengthen digital learning in EMRSs, smart classrooms, digital boards, computer labs with internet connectivity, and a dedicated DTH TV have been provided. Eklavya channel provides curriculum-based learning and competitive exam content for Classes 9th to 12th, ensuring continuous access to quality educational resources. At present there are 284 Smart classrooms in EMRSs across the country including the blocks of Sohagpur, Jaitpur, Anuppur and Umaria located in Shahdol Lok Sabha Constituency.

Further, National Education Society for Tribal Students (NESTS) continuously follows up with the State Governments and the execution agencies to expedite construction of EMRSs and to make them functional at the earliest. Besides, State Governments have also been advised to make the EMRS functional in alternate buildings, wherever feasible.

To strengthen the governance, management and operation of Eklavya Model Residential Schools (EMRSs), various institutional reforms have been taken such as;

  • Establishment of National Education Society for Tribal Students (NESTS) as an autonomous organization under the Ministry of Tribal Affairs to provide overall policy direction, academic support, monitoring, capacity building, recruitment, standardization of processes and implementation of the EMRS Scheme across the country;
  • State EMRS Societies to oversee the implementation, administration and day-to-day management of EMRSs within their jurisdictions;
  • District Level EMRS Committees, under the Chairmanship of the District Collector/District Magistrates to strengthen local oversight and resolve local implementation issues.
  • Comprehensive operational guidelines and circulars covering academic administration, financial management, procurement, student welfare, health and safety, hostel management, and grievance redressal to ensure uniform standards across all EMRSs.
  • Centralized recruitment mechanism through the EMRS Staff Selection Examination (ESSE) has been instituted to ensure the appointment of qualified and competent teaching and non-teaching personnel across EMRSs.
  • Structured induction programmes, regular in-service training, and continuous capacity-building initiatives to enhance professional competencies and strengthen institutional effectiveness.
  • In order to provide timely funds to EMRSs, NESTS is releasing recurring grant directly to the schools.

These institutional reforms have strengthened accountability, coordination, monitoring and thereby improving overall management of EMRSs.The State-wise details of sanctioned, operational and construction status of EMRSs, including Odisha, Bihar and Madhya Pradesh, are at Annexure I.

The details of sanctioned, operational and construction status of EMRSs in Keonjhar and Shahdol Parliament Constituency are at Annexure II.

None of the blocks in Araria Lok Sabha Constituency fulfill the prescribed criteria for establishing EMRS.

Total fund released for EMRS scheme to State of Odisha during last 5 years is Rs. 2254.71 Crore.

To address the issue of vacancies, 9111 teaching & non -teaching staff have already been recruited and examination has been conducted for another batch of 7267 teaching & non -teaching staff for EMRSs across the country. Total 514 teaching staff have been posted in EMRSs across Odisha in first phase of recruitment including 59 teaching staff in EMRSs in Keonjhar Lok Sabha constituency. In addition, State Governments have also been advised to depute staff on deputation and contract basis to address the issue of vacancies so that academic activities are not hampered.

EMRSs are well equipped with modern design with separate Boys’ and Girls’ Hostels, integrated dining and kitchen facilities, quarters for teaching and non-teaching staff, well-ventilated classrooms with modern teaching aids, science and computer laboratories, libraries with diverse learning resources, playgrounds and sports equipment, facilities for extracurricular activities like music, art and sports to preserve local art and culture.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Tribal Affairs
EVICTION OF TRIBAL COMMUNITIES
Posted On: 30 JUL 2026 1:38PM by PIB Delhi

Replying to a question in Lok Sabha today the Union Minister of State for Tribal Affairs Shri Durgadas Uikey informed that the representations that were received in the Ministry from Van Gujjar communities of Uttarakhand, Himachal Pradesh and Uttar Pradesh concerning the issues related to rights under the Scheduled Tribes and Other Traditional Forest Dwellers (Recognition of Forest Rights) Act, (in short FRA), 2006, were examined. Since the implementation of the FRA lies with the State Governments and UT Administrations, these representations were forwarded to the respective State Governments and concerned District Administrations for examination and taking necessary action in accordance with the provisions of the FRA and other applicable laws.

The Ministry of Tribal Affairs has been exhorting all State Governments/UT Administration to abide by the provisions contained in FRA. Regular review meetings to assess the progress of FRA etc are held with State Governments/UT Administration. Further, grievances /representations received in the Ministry regarding violation of provisions of FRA are forwarded to the States/UTs concerned, to ensure that legitimate claimants are not denied their forest rights.

Ministry of Tribal Affairs has advised States/UTs to undertake periodic training of Sub-Divisional Level Committee (SDLC) / District Level Committee (DLC) members and to ensure adherence to due process under the FRA. All training modules/ pamphlets are regularly shared with States/UTs. Capacity Building and training measures are being undertaken by State Governments/UT Administrations.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Tribal Affairs
TRIFED PROCUREMENT OF MFP
Posted On: 30 JUL 2026 1:36PM by PIB Delhi

Replying to a question in Lok Sabha today the Union Minister of State for Tribal Affairs Shri Durgadas Uikey informed that the Ministry of Tribal Affairs implements Pradhan Mantri Janjatiya Vikas Mission (PMJVM) scheme through Tribal Cooperative Marketing Development Federation of India Limited (TRIFED) for livelihood generation of the tribal beneficiaries across the country. Under the scheme, TRIFED is engaged in generating livelihood opportunities for tribal communities through marketing development of the tribal products produced by them which include handicraft, handloom & natural and food products. The identification and empanelment of tribal artisans and procurement of various tribal products from them are the core activities for generating livelihood opportunities for tribal communities. The various tribal products are sold through retail network chain of 115 Tribes India Outlets, exhibition and E-Commerce platforms. item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Tribal Affairs
EXPANSION OF EMRS IN WEST BENGAL
Posted On: 30 JUL 2026 1:35PM by PIB Delhi

Replying to a question in Lok Sabha today the Union Minister of State for Tribal Affairs Shri Durgadas Uikey informed that Bundwan block of Purulia district in West Bengal is the only block meeting the prescribed criteria for establishment of Eklavya Model Residential School (EMRS). The land for said block has been identified by State Government.

As reported by the State Government, EMRS in Kalimpong is functional in alternate building and the construction of permanent building has commenced. A total of Rs 20.91 Cr has been approved for EMRS Kalimpong out of which Rs. 9.96 Cr has been released.

Under the existing scheme, the establishment of EMRS is based on 2011 census.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Tribal Affairs
Implementation of DAJGUA in Himachal Pradesh
Posted On: 30 JUL 2026 1:34PM by PIB Delhi

Replying to a question in Lok Sabha today the Union Minister of State for Tribal Affairs Shri Durgadas Uikey informed that there are 156 villages in 7 blocks have been identified for development under the Dharti Aaba Janjatiya Gram Utkarsh Abhiyan (DAJGUA) for tribal development in Chamba district of Himachal Pradesh.

The Chamba District, Himachal Pradesh has two Integrated Tribal Development Projects (ITDPs), namely ITDP Bharmour and ITDP Pangi. Under the Dharti Aaba Janjatiya Gram Utkarsh Abhiyan (DAJGUA), 30 villages in ITDP Bharmour and 48 villages in ITDP Pangi have been selected for coverage. Under the interventions of the Ministry of Tribal Affairs (MoTA), Government of India, projects amounting to ₹551.11 lakh in ITDP Bharmour and ₹851.00 lakh in ITDP Pangi have been approved so far.

The details of funds released to Chamba district under DAJGUA (in lakhs rupees) is at Annexure I.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Tribal Affairs
PROGRESS UNDER PM-JANMAN
Posted On: 30 JUL 2026 1:32PM by PIB Delhi

Replying to a question in Lok Sabha today the Union Minister of State for Tribal Affairs Shri Durgadas Uikey informed that Pradhan Mantri Janjati Adivasi Nyaya Maha Abhiyan (PM JANMAN) was launched by the Hon'ble Prime Minister on 15th November, 2023 for the socio-economic development of the 75 Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Group (PVTG) communities residing in 18 States including Gujarat and one Union Territory.

The mission aims to provide basic facilities to improve their socio-economic conditions such as safe housing, clean drinking water and improved access to education, health and nutrition, road and telecom connectivity, electrification of unelectrified households and sustainable livelihood opportunities. These objectives are being met through 11 interventions implemented by 9-line Ministries. The details of the benefits given under PM JANMAN, as on 30.06.2026, Ministry-wise & State-wise and District-wise in Gujarat, are given at Annexure I. The progress so made under the abhiyan has contributed to the socio-economic development of PVTGs through improvement in basic amenities and livelihood opportunities.

Ministry of Tribal Affairs through the State Governments/UT Administration/departments has undertaken habitation level data collection exercise through PM Gati Shakti mobile application to estimate PVTG population figures and infrastructure gaps in order to cover PVTG population residing in villages & habitations covered under PM JANMAN. Based on the data captured, State/UT- wise, PVTG villages, habitations and population is tabulated at Annexure II. The actual number beneficiaries to be covered under the abhiyan is subjected to eligibility criteria of specific guidelines of concerned interventions as per norms approved.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Tribal Affairs
Development of Areas under Integrated Tribal Development Agency
Posted On: 30 JUL 2026 1:30PM by PIB Delhi

Union Minister Shri Jual Oram has laid a statement on the Table of the House today.

STATEMENT REFERRED TO DEVELOPMENT OF AREAS UNDER INTEGRATED TRIBAL DEVELOPMENT AGENCY

The Union Government supports development in ITDA/ITDP areas through various schemes and programmes of the Ministry of Tribal Affairs and other sectoral Ministries. Assistance is provided, inter alia, under Grants under Article 275(1) of the Constitution, Pradhan Mantri Adi Adarsh Gram Yojana/State Tribal Sub-Plan support, PM-JANMAN, Dharti Aaba Janjatiya Gram Utkarsh Abhiyan (DA-JGUA), Eklavya Model Residential Schools, PM-JANMAN, scholarship schemes and tribal livelihood programmes. Grants under Article 275(1) are provided to bridge critical gaps in sectors such as education, health, agriculture and infrastructure. ITDAs/ITDPs function as important field-level institutions for convergence and implementation of these interventions.

Funds under the aforesaid schemes are generally allocated and released State-wise and scheme-wise, and not separately for each ITDA/ITDP area. Releases are made on the basis of approved proposals, availability of funds, utilisation certificates and compliance with scheme guidelines. The State-wise details of funds released during the last five years, including for Andhra Pradesh is at Annexure-I.

The implementation of Central interventions is reviewed regularly through meetings with States/UTs, field visits, scheme dashboards, physical and financial progress reports and outcome-based monitoring. Further, a National Conclave on Strengthening of ITDAs and ITDPs was organised on 3 June, 2026 to assess institutional capacity, convergence, planning and last-mile service delivery. The deliberations highlighted the need for stronger staffing, integrated planning, reliable data systems, community participation, improved convergence with line departments and greater functional and financial empowerment of ITDAs/ITDPs.

The Government is implementing a convergence-based approach in ITDA areas covering:

(i) Roads, housing, drinking water, electricity, mobile connectivity and other basic infrastructure under DA-JGUA, PM-JANMAN and schemes of the concerned line Ministries;

(ii) Establishment and strengthening of Eklavya Model Residential Schools, hostels, scholarships and other educational facilities;

(iii) Healthcare interventions, including mobile medical units, health screening, maternal and child healthcare and the National Sickle Cell Anaemia Elimination Mission;

(iv) Promotion of agriculture, horticulture, minor forest produce, Van Dhan Vikas Kendras, tribal enterprises and market linkages; and

(v) Skill development, capacity building and livelihood training through convergence with the concerned Ministries and State Governments.

 

(e)        Creation, reorganization or expansion of ITDAs/ITDPs is considered on the basis of proposals received from the respective State Government/UT Administration and their conformity with the prescribed criteria.

item.title: Raksha Mantri felicitates crew of IASV Triveni for completing first-ever all-women Tri-services circumnavigation sailing expedition
item.dc:creator: Ministry of Defence
item.description: Ministry of Defence Raksha Mantri felicitates crew of IASV Triveni for completing first-ever all-women Tri-services circumnavigation sailing expedition Samudra Pradakshina is proof of Tri-service jointness & Nari Shakti, it will inspire every Indian: Shri Rajnath Singh Posted On: 30 JUL 2026 1:12PM by PIB Delhi Raksha Mantri Shri Rajnath Singh, on July 30, 2026, felicitated the nine women officers of the three Services, who returned home after successfully completing the first-ever Tri-service all-women circumnavigation sailing expedition ‘Samudra Pradakshina’ onboard…
item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Defence
Raksha Mantri felicitates crew of IASV Triveni for completing first-ever all-women Tri-services circumnavigation sailing expedition
Samudra Pradakshina is proof of Tri-service jointness & Nari Shakti, it will inspire every Indian: Shri Rajnath Singh
Posted On: 30 JUL 2026 1:12PM by PIB Delhi

Raksha Mantri Shri Rajnath Singh, on July 30, 2026, felicitated the nine women officers of the three Services, who returned home after successfully completing the first-ever Tri-service all-women circumnavigation sailing expedition ‘Samudra Pradakshina’ onboard the Indian Army Sailing Vessel (IASV) Triveni. Interacting with the officers in New Delhi, Raksha Mantri praised the team's courage and determination in successfully completing the 314-day voyage covering nearly 25,500 nautical miles across four oceans. He described the expedition as a testament to Nari Shakti and an outstanding example of Tri-service jointness & synergy that will inspire every Indian.

The women officers shared their experiences with Shri Rajnath Singh, highlighting that the expedition’s demanding nature made the voyage both memorable and rewarding. They said that their unwavering commitment to making the nation proud kept them motivated, enabling them to overcome immense physical and mental challenges. Raksha Mantri remarked that their dedication had inspired him and reinforced his own resolve. He added that their achievement demonstrates how firm conviction and determination can help one accomplish any goal in life.

Describing the officers’ capability and confidence as “incredible”, Shri Rajnath Singh asserted that the successful completion of ‘Samudra Pradakshina’ shattered the stereotypes that claimed that women cannot accomplish arduous military missions. “You have proven that physical capability, mental toughness, and leadership qualities are not bound by gender. Every daughter in India can look at you and believe that she, too, can cross oceans and conquer the world,” he told the officers.

Raksha Mantri termed the expedition as a shining example of ‘Tri-service Jointness’. He noted that officers from the Indian Army, Indian Navy and Indian Air Force sailed together on the same vessel under the same flag in pursuit of a shared mission. “The expedition is a testament to the fact that no horizon is too vast to conquer if we move forward together,” he added.

 

Shri Rajnath Singh commended the team for showcasing India's engineering excellence, indigenous capabilities and technological advancements to the countries they visited, stating that "you conveyed a message to the world that India is second to none in any field."

Chief of the Army Staff General Dhiraj Seth, Defence Secretary Shri Rajesh Kumar Singh, Vice Chief of the Air Staff Air Marshal Ashutosh Dixit, Vice Chief of the Naval Staff Vice Admiral Ajay Kochhar and other senior officers of three Services were present during the interaction.

The team of IASV Triveni was virtually flagged-in by Raksha Mantri on July 22, 2026 in Mumbai. He had graced the flag-off ceremony on September 11, 2025 through video conferencing.

The success of the mission was made possible through meticulous planning, nearly two years of intensive training, a dedicated 24X7 shore-based support network and the unwavering commitment of numerous organisations and support agencies. The expedition successfully fulfilled all internationally recognised criteria for a circumnavigation by crossing all meridians of longitude, crossing the Equator twice, crossing the International Date Line and rounding the Three Great Capes - Cape Leeuwin, Cape Horn and the Cape of Good Hope.

The successful passage through the formidable Drake Passage and rounding of Cape Horn earned the crew membership of the prestigious fraternity of Cape Horners, an honour reserved for sailors who conquer one of the world’s most demanding maritime passages.

Beyond its remarkable maritime achievement, ‘Samudra Pradakshina’ also served as a powerful instrument of military diplomacy. During port calls across the globe, IASV Triveni showcased India's rich cultural heritage, maritime traditions, military professionalism and enduring values while strengthening goodwill with friendly nations.

item.description: Ministry of Commerce & Industry India rises from 82nd to 57th in global rankings, in structural and pro-competitive reforms: Report by Competere Foundation Improved ranking reflects progress in reducing market distortions and strengthening competitiveness between 2010 and 2023: CTIL Posted On: 30 JUL 2026 12:09PM by PIB Delhi India has advanced 25 places in the global rankings, from 82nd to 57th, reflecting significant progress in structural and pro-competitive reforms between 2010 and 2023, according to the report India's Next Growth Frontier: Reducing…
item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Commerce & Industry
India rises from 82nd to 57th in global rankings, in structural and pro-competitive reforms: Report by Competere Foundation
Improved ranking reflects progress in reducing market distortions and strengthening competitiveness between 2010 and 2023: CTIL
Posted On: 30 JUL 2026 12:09PM by PIB Delhi

India has advanced 25 places in the global rankings, from 82nd to 57th, reflecting significant progress in structural and pro-competitive reforms between 2010 and 2023, according to the report India's Next Growth Frontier: Reducing Anti-Competitive Market Distortions to Build on India's 2010–2023 Reform Progress, released by the Competere Foundation. The report assesses India's performance under its Market Distortions Performance Index, examining the country's reform trajectory between 2010 and 2023, and attributes the improvement to sustained efforts in reducing market distortions and strengthening competitiveness.

The report was launched during a discussion on "India's Reform Trajectory, Market Distortions and the Next Frontier for Growth and Competitiveness", organised by the Centre for Trade and Investment Law (CTIL), Indian Institute of Foreign Trade (IIFT), New Delhi, in collaboration with the Competere Foundation for Trade and Competition Policy, at the India Habitat Centre, New Delhi. The discussion focused on India's structural reform journey, policy measures to enhance competitiveness, and the next phase of reforms required to sustain growth in an evolving global trade environment.

The report evaluates market distortions across three broad pillars—property rights protection, domestic competition and international competition. It highlights reforms such as the implementation of the Goods and Services Tax (GST), the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code (IBC), improvements in the regulatory environment and the modernisation of trade facilitation systems. It also examines developments relating to competition, investment conditions, digital markets and external regulatory barriers affecting India's competitiveness and participation in international trade.

The inaugural session commenced with welcome remarks by Professor and Head, Centre for Trade and Investment Law (CTIL), Dr James J. Nedumpara, who highlighted the importance of assessing India's reform trajectory in the context of global competitiveness and international trade.

State Election Commissioner of the Union Territory of Ladakh and Former Secretary, Government of India, Shri Sudhanshu Pandey, delivered the keynote address. This was followed by a presentation on the report's key findings by Chairman and President of the Competere Foundation for Trade and Competition Policy, Mr Shanker Singham.

The report also underlines the importance of maintaining an evidence-based and effects-oriented approach to competition policy, reviewing sector-specific investment restrictions in light of consumer welfare outcomes and strengthening cooperation with like-minded trading partners to address regulatory barriers in international markets.

A panel discussion brought together experts from the legal, industry, academic and policy communities to deliberate on India's reform experience, competition policy, investment climate, market distortions and emerging challenges in international trade. The programme concluded with an interactive question-and-answer session.

The event brought together representatives from the legal, academic, industry and policy communities to discuss policy measures for strengthening India's competitiveness, productivity and integration with the global economy.

item.content:encoded:
PIB Backgrounder
Affordable Nutrition for Every Indian: Jan Aushadhi Nutraceuticals
Posted On: 30 JUL 2026 11:05AM by PIB Delhi

In an increasingly health-conscious India, nutraceuticals have gained recognition as an essential part of overall well-being. Be it for school-going children or senior citizens, dietary supplements, herbal products that include vitamins & minerals, herbs & botanicals, probiotics, etc., have found wide acceptance.  Yet, affordability continues to be a challenge for millions of families seeking nutritional supplements. The Pradhan Mantri Bhartiya Janaushadhi Pariyojana (PMBJP) is addressing this gap with its nutraceutical basket. From nutrition bars to disease-specific formulations, the Jan Aushadhi nutraceuticals Basket is making nutrition supplements more accessible to people across India.

Nutrition for Diverse Needs

The Jan Aushadhi portfolio is designed to respond to the varied needs of young, old, women, and people with different health issues. The range includes protein supplements, immunity products, nutritional foods and specialised formulations for individuals with specific dietary requirements.

Manufactured in accordance with prescribed quality standards and offered at affordable prices, these products aim to make regular nutritional support more accessible without placing an undue burden on household budgets.

Convenient Nutrition for Active Lifestyles

Nutrient-dense Jan Aushadhi Protein Bar & Jan Aushadhi Immunity Bar offer a portable source of nourishment for children, working professionals and fitness enthusiasts. Available in chocolate flavour in a 35-gram pack, protein bar provides a convenient way to supplement daily protein intake while on the go. Enriched with Immunity-Supporting Ingredients tasty Immunity Bar provides energy and strengthens body’s protective barriers. These nutrition bars offer an economical alternative for consumers craving a quick snack but averse to junk food.

For a more substantial protein supplement, 100% Whey Protein Powder & Jan Aushadhi Protein Powder support daily protein intake and muscle recovery, making it suitable for fitness enthusiasts. Protein Powder is available in Vanilla and Kesar Pista flavours, giving consumers greater choice.

Supporting Women's Nutritional Needs

Women have distinct nutritional requirements at different stages of life.  Jan Aushadhi Women Protein Boost is formulated to support daily protein intake, energy levels, and healthy bones and muscles. Available in chocolate and vanilla flavours, the 250-gram pack is priced at ₹204.66. By offering specialised nutrition at affordable rates, this product seeks to make it easier for more women to incorporate nutritional supplementation into their daily routines.

Nutrition Designed for Specific Health Needs

For individuals managing specific health conditions such as Diabetes, Kidney problems etc, dietary requirements can be more complex. Diabetes Care Protein Powder from JanAushadhi complements the nutritional requirements of people living with diabetes. For individuals with kidney-related conditions, Renal Care Protein Powder is available in both Low Protein and High Protein variants, allowing the choice of formulation to be guided by medical advice and individual dietary needs.

Jan Aushadhi Poshan: Everyday Nutrition for Families

For affordable everyday nutritional support for everyone in the family, the Jan Aushadhi Poshan range offers malt-based nutritional food enriched with essential vitamins and minerals.

Available in regular malt and cocoa variants, the range includes:

  • Malt Based Food, 500 g: ₹160.17
  • Malt Based Food with Cocoa, 500 g: ₹164.62
  • Malt Based Food with Cocoa Sachet, 30 g: ₹8.90

The multiple pack sizes offer flexibility for different consumption needs and budgets. Easy to prepare and suitable for regular consumption, the Poshan range provides families with an accessible nutritional supplement for everyday use.

Making Quality Nutrition More Accessible

These products highlight the growing importance of nutrition as part of a broader approach to health management. While specialised nutritional products should be used in accordance with professional medical and dietary guidance, affordable access can help make appropriate nutritional support more attainable for families. For overall well-being, lifestyle choices that include quality nutrition cannot be stressed more.  Families are increasingly opting to make healthy choices when it comes to food and nutrition supplements. By offering affordable alternatives to expensive branded nutrition supplements through the Jan Aushadhi Kendra network, PMBJP is ensuring that quality nutritional support is not limited by income.

Affordable medicines remain the core of PMBJP, but nutrition is an essential part of the same larger health journey. Whether it is a student seeking convenient nourishment, a working professional managing a demanding routine, a homemaker supporting family nutrition, a senior citizen with specific dietary needs or an individual managing a health condition, access to appropriate nutrition can play an important role in supporting well-being.

By combining quality, affordability and accessibility, the Jan Aushadhi nutraceutical range is helping make nutrition a more attainable choice for Indian families reinforcing the vision of “Quality Healthcare and Nutrition for All.”

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Science & Technology
TDB-DST supports M/s Sonic Biochem Extractions Pvt. Ltd., Indore, for Commercialization of Indigenous Functional and Textured Soya Protein Concentrates
Posted On: 30 JUL 2026 10:57AM by PIB Delhi

Reinforcing India's commitment to self-reliance in value-added food processing and plant-based nutrition, the Technology Development Board (TDB), under the Department of Science & Technology (DST), Government of India, has extended financial assistance to M/s Sonic Biochem Extractions Pvt. Ltd., Indore (Madhya Pradesh) for the project titled “Development & Commercialization of Functional and Textured Soya Protein Concentrate(s).” The project aims to establish a state-of-the-art manufacturing facility for the commercial production of Functional Soya Protein Concentrate (FSPC) and Textured Soya Protein Concentrate (TSPC) using indigenous technology developed by the company.

The initiative addresses the growing global demand for high-quality, non-GMO plant-based protein ingredients driven by increasing consumer preference for healthy, sustainable, and clean-label food products. It also aligns with the Government of India's vision of strengthening domestic food processing capabilities, promoting value addition in agriculture, and advancing Aatmanirbhar Bharat through import substitution and export-oriented manufacturing.

With over two decades of experience in manufacturing and exporting non-GMO soya food ingredients, Sonic Biochem has developed an indigenous process for producing both FSPC and TSPC using Soya Protein Concentrate (SPC) as the primary raw material. Unlike conventional manufacturing processes that depend on comparatively expensive Soya Protein Isolate (SPI)—largely imported from countries such as China and the United States—the company's technology utilizes SPC indigenously developed and manufactured in-house while delivering comparable functional properties. This innovation significantly reduces production costs, enhances competitiveness, and strengthens India's self-reliance in the plant protein sector.

The project will establish commercial-scale manufacturing capacity for these advanced protein ingredients, which find extensive applications across processed foods, plant-based meat alternatives, nutritional supplements, and functional food products. The technology is expected to reduce import dependence, generate new export opportunities, and strengthen India's position in the rapidly expanding global market for value-added plant proteins.

By leveraging indigenous technology and locally sourced non-GMO soybeans, the project will create a robust domestic value chain for high-value protein ingredients while providing Indian food manufacturers with affordable access to globally competitive raw materials. The initiative is also expected to contribute to higher value realization for the agricultural sector and support the country's transition towards sustainable food systems.

Speaking on the occasion, Shri Rajesh Kumar Pathak, Secretary, TDB, stated, "Development of indigenous manufacturing capabilities for advanced plant protein ingredients is strategically important for strengthening India's food processing sector and expanding our presence in global markets. TDB remains committed to supporting technologies that promote value addition, reduce import dependence, and create globally competitive products under the vision of Aatmanirbhar Bharat. This initiative is expected to generate significant foreign exchange savings while creating new export opportunities for India."

Expressing gratitude for the support, the leadership of M/s Sonic Biochem Extractions Pvt. Ltd. stated that the assistance from TDB will enable the company to commercialize its indigenously developed technology at scale, strengthen India's leadership in non-GMO soya protein ingredients, and cater to the growing domestic and international demand for sustainable, high-quality plant-based nutrition solutions.

Prime Minister's Office
Prime Minister shares Sanskrit Subhashitam highlighting respect for nature and environmental stewardship
Posted On: 30 JUL 2026 10:26AM by PIB Delhi

The Prime Minister, Shri Narendra Modi, said that respect for nature, the environment and the entire creation lies at the very core of our existence. He called upon everyone to participate, with a spirit of gratitude and selfless service towards nature, in building a healthy, prosperous and strong nation.

The Prime Minister shared a Sanskrit Subhashitam-

“शं नो द्यावापृथिवी पूर्वहूतौ शमन्तरिक्षं दृशये नो अस्तु।

शं न ओषधीर्वनिनो भवन्तु शं नो रजसस्पतिरस्तु जिष्णुः॥”

The Subhashitam conveys that May Dyuloka and the Earth, which have been revered since the beginning of creation, always be auspicious for us. May the intermediate space between the Earth and the Sun be beneficial and enlightening for our lives. May all medicinal herbs and forest plants provide us with health, nourishment, and happiness. May the all-pervading and victorious Lord of all worlds ever grant us welfare, peace, and prosperity.

The Prime Minister wrote on X;

“प्रकृति, पर्यावरण और समस्त सृष्टि का सम्मान हमारे अस्तित्व के मूल में है। आइए, हम इनके प्रति पूरी कृतज्ञता और सेवाभाव के साथ एक स्वस्थ, समृद्ध और सशक्त राष्ट्र के निर्माण में सहभागी बनें।

शं न ओषधीर्वनिनो भवन्तु शं नो रजसस्पतिरस्तु जिष्णुः॥”

item.title: Minister Ram Mohan Naidu reviews India’s preparedness for SAF and CORSIA implementation
item.dc:creator: Ministry of Civil Aviation
item.description: Ministry of Civil Aviation Minister Ram Mohan Naidu reviews India’s preparedness for SAF and CORSIA implementation Chairs high-level stakeholder meeting on SAF production, blending roadmap and carbon accounting framework Posted On: 29 JUL 2026 9:55PM by PIB Delhi The Ministry of Civil Aviation today organized a high-level stakeholder meeting chaired by Minister Ram Mohan Naidu to review India's preparedness for the adoption of Sustainable Aviation Fuel (SAF) and compliance with the Carbon Offsetting and Reduction Scheme for International Aviation (CORSIA), the global…
item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Civil Aviation
Minister Ram Mohan Naidu reviews India’s preparedness for SAF and CORSIA implementation
Chairs high-level stakeholder meeting on SAF production, blending roadmap and carbon accounting framework
Posted On: 29 JUL 2026 9:55PM by PIB Delhi

The Ministry of Civil Aviation today organized a high-level stakeholder meeting chaired by Minister Ram Mohan Naidu to review India's preparedness for the adoption of Sustainable Aviation Fuel (SAF) and compliance with the Carbon Offsetting and Reduction Scheme for International Aviation (CORSIA), the global carbon reduction framework of the International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO).

The meeting was attended by Secretary (Civil Aviation) and senior officials from the Ministry of Civil Aviation, Ministry of Petroleum & Natural Gas, Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change, Directorate General of Civil Aviation (DGCA), Airports Authority of India (AAI), Bureau of Indian Standards (BIS), Bureau of Energy Efficiency (BEE), Oil Marketing Companies (OMCs), airlines, airport operators and other key stakeholders.

The meeting reviewed the progress made in SAF production, certification, and supply chain development across the country. The status of various SAF production projects being implemented by Oil Marketing Companies and the timelines for commissioning these facilities were also reviewed. Stakeholders deliberated on measures required to ensure the timely availability of Sustainable Aviation Fuel to meet the anticipated demand from 2027 onwards.

Speaking on the occasion, Minister for Civil Aviation Shri Ram Mohan Naidu said, “India is committed to building a robust and globally competitive Sustainable Aviation Fuel ecosystem that supports the growth of our aviation sector while contributing meaningfully to global decarbonisation efforts. Guided by Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi’s vision of ‘One Earth, One Family, One Future’, we are approaching SAF not merely as a compliance requirement but as a strategic national opportunity. Multiple stakeholders including the farmers stand to gain from the SAF value chain.”

The Minister further stated, “As an industry, we are already working on multiple fronts to reduce emissions. From 0 in 2014, today 104 airports in the country have switched entirely to 100% green energy usage. By encouraging the leasing ecosystem, airlines are being supported to have modern and fuel-efficient fleets. SAF is also a critical component for our collective efforts. We must now move from feasibility studies to concrete production timelines and from ambition to action. Every stakeholder needs to have clear obligations for ensuring adequate production as well as robust accounting. Our immediate priority is to achieve the 1% CORSIA blending requirement in the most cost-effective manner. As part of our long-term strategy, the carbon-credit offset mechanism must be developed through a whole-of-government approach.”

Shri Ram Mohan Naidu reviewed the proposed implementation roadmap for SAF blending mandate, including the roles and responsibilities of Oil Marketing Companies, airlines and airport operators. Discussions were held on establishing a robust accounting, monitoring and reporting framework aligned with ICAO/CORSIA requirements, development of a national SAF Registry with end-to-end traceability and measures to facilitate certification and market access.

Emphasising the importance of coordinated execution, the Minister said, “This transition must be driven through collective decision-making and close coordination among all stakeholders. We reviewed progress in SAF supply-chain development, the national SAF Registry, accounting and reporting systems and measures required for effective CORSIA compliance. I am encouraged by the significant progress already made and by the commitment shown by all participating Ministries and industry stakeholders. We have directed all concerned stakeholders to expedite the identified action points so that India is fully prepared well before the mandatory phase of CORSIA begins on 1 January 2027.”

Talking about the SAF Policy and the financial impact of SAF, Minister added, “The draft SAF policy is now in its final stages. So, we are doing multiple such inter-ministerial consultations and stakeholder engagements at various levels. For me voice of the passenger remains central and passenger happen to be the most important stakeholder of our industry. We have to ensure that this process imposes the least possible burden on passengers and airlines. For that we need to study all the possible SAF pathways and within pathways identify the most cost-effective mechanism right from production to drop-in at the airport”.

The meeting further deliberated on India's preparedness for CORSIA implementation, including the issuance of Letters of Authorisation and the development of a CORSIA-compliant carbon market framework in India.

The Government of India remains committed to promoting domestic production of Sustainable Aviation Fuel, strengthening India's aviation ecosystem, reducing carbon emissions from international aviation and positioning India as a global leader in sustainable aviation.

***

Divyanshu Kumar

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Communications
Union Minister of Communications Shri Jyotiraditya M. Scindia Unveils Theme for 10th Edition of India Mobile Congress 2026: ‘Scale without boundaries’
IMC 2026 to Bring Together Global Technology Leaders, Innovators, Startups and Policymakers to Shape the Next Phase of India’s Digital Transformation
Posted On: 29 JUL 2026 9:39PM by PIB Delhi

Shri Jyotiraditya M. Scindia, Union Minister for Communications and Development of North Eastern Region, today unveiled “Scale without boundaries” as the theme for the 10th edition of India Mobile Congress (IMC) 2026. The landmark edition of Asia’s largest digital technology forum is scheduled to be held from October 7–10, 2026, at Yashobhoomi (India International Convention & Expo Centre), New Delhi.

The theme launch event was also graced by Dr. Chandra Sekhar Pemmasani, Union Minister of State for Communications & Rural Development as the Guest of Honour, and Shri Amit Agrawal, Secretary, Department of Telecommunications (DoT), Ministry of Communications as the Special Guest.

The theme “Scale without boundaries” reflects India’s ambition to build a digital future where technology, innovation and connectivity transcend traditional boundaries and reach every sector, community and region. It underscores the need to take transformative technologies and solutions beyond experimentation and enable their widespread adoption, integration and impact at scale. The theme also highlights the importance of fostering collaboration among technology, infrastructure, industry, startups, academia, policymakers and consumers to create an ecosystem where innovation can scale without limitations and contribute meaningfully to inclusive growth and national development.

The 10th edition of India Mobile Congress (IMC) 2026 is anchored around four key pillars that reflect India’s vision of building a digitally empowered, secure and growth-oriented future:-

  1. Srishti – Building the Future, which will focus on fostering innovation, emerging technologies and solutions that shape the next generation of digital infrastructure.
  2. Suraksha – Strengthening Trust, which will underscore the importance of secure, resilient and trusted digital ecosystems.
  3. Sashakt – Expanding Opportunities, aimed at leveraging technology to empower citizens, businesses, startups and communities while ensuring inclusive access to digital opportunities.
  4. Samvardhan – Fueling Growth, which will highlight the role of digital technologies in driving economic growth, investment, entrepreneurship, job creation and India’s emergence as a global technology leader.

Together, these four pillars embody the spirit of “Scale without boundaries”, reflecting the ambition to take innovation, connectivity and digital transformation beyond boundaries and enable their impact to scale across sectors, geographies and communities.

As India advances towards a digitally empowered and technology-driven future, IMC 2026 will provide a platform to explore how emerging technologies and robust digital infrastructure can enable scale across sectors and geographies. The event will spotlight the convergence of technologies such as 5G, 6G, Artificial Intelligence, Internet of Things, cloud and edge computing, satellite communications, electronics manufacturing, quantum technologies and green technologies, among others.

Speaking on the occasion, Shri Jyotiraditya M. Scindia, Union Minister for Communications and Development of North Eastern Region, said that “India’s journey in telecom has moved from connecting the next billion to enabling the next billion possibilities. The theme of the 10th India Mobile Congress, ‘Scale Without Boundaries’, reflects our ambition to ensure that the technologies we build, the standards we shape and the solutions we create in India reach new markets, communities and possibilities across the world.”

The Union Minister further emphasised that “India is no longer only a market for technology; we are increasingly becoming a nation that designs, develops and scales technology for the world. From indigenous telecom technologies and 6G standards to digital public platforms, our journey from ‘Vocal for Local’ to ‘Local for Global’ embodies the spirit of ‘Scale without Boundaries’ and our vision of building a Viksit Bharat 2047.”

Echoing the vision outlined by the Union Minister, Dr. Chandra Sekhar Pemmasani, Union Minister of State for Communications & Rural Development, said that “The last 10 years has been unprecedented for Indian Telecom. IMC is an event which help us showcase to the world what India has achieved in the field of telecom. This is a place where government gets an opportunity to collaborate, startups showcase their hard work and investors find opportunities to invest.”

Highlighting the significance of the 10th edition of India Mobile Congress, Shri Amit Agrawal, Chairman, Digital Communications Commission and Secretary, Department of Telecommunications (DoT), stated that “It is a privilege to be here at 10th Edition of IMC and the journey of 10 years. This time, we are going with a much larger strategy and will showcase India’s progress in the field of telecom to the world.”

Organised by the Department of Telecommunications (DoT) and the Cellular Operators Association of India (COAI), IMC 2026 will bring together leading global and Indian technology companies, telecom operators, policymakers, startups, investors, researchers and innovators under one platform. The 10th edition will build upon the success of previous editions and further strengthen IMC’s position as a premier global forum for discussions on the future of telecommunications and digital technologies.

The event will showcase cutting-edge innovations and use cases across emerging technologies, while providing a platform for technology demonstrations, product launches, industry collaborations, investment opportunities, knowledge exchange and policy dialogue. The flagship start-up programme ASPIRE will continue to provide emerging technology startups with opportunities to connect with investors, incubators, accelerators, industry leaders and potential partners.

With its 10th edition, IMC 2026 aims to move beyond showcasing technological advancements to examining how these innovations can be integrated, scaled and translated into real-world outcomes. The event will focus on building resilient and inclusive digital ecosystems that can empower citizens, strengthen industries, create new opportunities and accelerate India’s emergence as a global technology leader.

Marking a decade of India Mobile Congress, the 10th edition celebrates a remarkable journey that began with the aspiration to “connect the next billion”. Over the past ten years, IMC has evolved alongside India’s telecom and digital transformation, providing a platform for innovation, collaboration and global engagement. As India enters the next decade, IMC 2026 looks ahead to a larger ambition — taking Indian technologies, standards and solutions beyond boundaries and connecting the next possibilities.

The previous editions of India Mobile Congress was a huge success with over 1.4 lakh visitors, 860 exhibitors, representatives from 101countries, 1,500 Use Cases showcased, 465 startups participated, featured 918 speakers across 113 sessions, including 52 keynote addresses, 12 roundtables, and 84 panel discussions.

Ministry of Communications
Union Minister of Communications Shri Jyotiraditya M. Scindia confers Pandit Deendayal Upadhyaya Telecom Excellence Awards
Posted On: 29 JUL 2026 9:36PM by PIB Delhi

Union Minister of Communications and Development of North Eastern Region, Shri Jyotiraditya M. Scindia today conferred the Pandit Deendayal Upadhyaya Telecom Excellence Awards- 2025 to two organizations for their outstanding contributions in Telecom Technology. The awardees are as follows:

  1. Amantya Technologies Pvt. Ltd.
  2. Finaara

Union Minister of State for Communications and Rural Development, Dr. Chandra Sekhar Pemmasani, Secretary, Department of Telecommunications, Shri Amit Agrawal and other dignitaries attended the event.

Shri Scindia congratulated the awardees on winning the prestigious Pandit Deendayal Upadhyaya Telecom Excellence Awards.

The selection process for Pandit Deendayal Upadhyaya Telecom Excellence Awards included nomination by all Indian citizens as well as institutions registered in India through Rashtriya Puraskar Portal (https://awards.gov.in) managed by Director General, Awards at the Ministry of Home Affairs.

About Pandit Deendayal Upadhyaya Telecom Excellence Awards:

‘Pandit Deendayal Upadhyaya Telecom Excellence Awards’ have been instituted by Department of Telecommunications, Ministry of Communications, to encourage innovations in telecom sector and stimulate/ inspire Telecom Skill ecosystem by rewarding the successful telecom skilled people and institutions of India annually for their exemplary and outstanding contributions  in the areas of Telecom Innovations, Telecom Skilling, Telecom Services, Telecom Manufacturing, Telecom Applications in deploying telecom dependent sectoral solutions for different fields such as agriculture, commerce, health, education etc.
