The initiative aims to build a…
item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment
Government Strengthens Grassroots Drug Prevention Through Panchayati Raj Institutions Under Nasha Mukt Bharat Abhiyan
Panchayat Resource Persons Being Engaged as Nasha Mukti Mitras to Promote Drug-Free Villages
Posted On: 29 JUL 2026 6:38PM by PIB Delhi

The Government of India is strengthening grassroots efforts to combat drug abuse under the Nasha Mukt Bharat Abhiyan (NMBA) by promoting greater participation of Panchayati Raj Institutions in awareness generation and community mobilisation. The initiative aims to build a people-led movement against substance abuse by engaging local communities and volunteers at the village level.

This information was given by the Minister of State for Social Justice and Empowerment, Shri B. L. Verma, in a written reply to Shri Harsh Mahajan in the Rajya Sabha today.

The Minister informed that while no separate scheme has been formulated for convergence of Panchayati Raj Institutions with the National Action Plan for Drug Demand Reduction (NAPDDR) specifically for village-level drug awareness, all Panchayati Raj Departments of States and Union Territories, including Himachal Pradesh, have been requested under the Nasha Mukt Bharat Abhiyan to identify and engage Panchayat Resource Persons as Nasha Mukti Mitras (NMMs).

These Nasha Mukti Mitras have been entrusted with promoting the NMBA Mass Pledge against drug abuse through both online and offline campaigns. They are also being integrated into existing awareness drives and are promoting the use of the NMBA logo, mascot and the National De-addiction Helpline 14446 to strengthen outreach at the grassroots level.

The Minister further informed that under the State Action Plan (SAP) component of the NAPDDR Scheme, financial assistance is provided to State Governments and Union Territory Administrations for preventive education, awareness generation, capacity building and drug demand reduction activities. During the last two financial years, no funds were released to Himachal Pradesh in 2023–24 and 2024–25. However, ₹1.34 crore was released to the State during 2025–26 to support activities under the State Action Plan.

The Government continues to strengthen the Nasha Mukt Bharat Abhiyan through active participation of Panchayati Raj Institutions, community volunteers, educational institutions and civil society organisations to create sustained awareness against drug abuse and realise the vision of a Nasha Mukt Bharat.

item.title: Government Strengthens Implementation of SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act Through Timely Central Assistance to States and UTs
item.dc:creator: Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment
Government Strengthens Implementation of SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act Through Timely Central Assistance to States and UTs
Central-Level Committee Holds 29 Review Meetings Since 2006; ₹30.52 Crores Released to Telangana Under the Centrally Sponsored Scheme
Posted On: 29 JUL 2026 6:37PM by PIB Delhi

The Government of India continues to strengthen the implementation of the Scheduled Castes and the Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989 and the Protection of Civil Rights Act, 1955 through regular monitoring, timely financial assistance and close coordination with States and Union Territories under the Centrally Sponsored Scheme.

This information was given by Minister of State for Social Justice and Empowerment Shri Ramdas Athawale in a written reply Dr Mallu Ravi in the Lok Sabha.

The Minister informed that a Central-level Committee, constituted under the chairpersonship of the Union Minister for Social Justice and Empowerment on 29 March 2006, regularly reviews the implementation of the Scheme and the provisions of the two Acts. Since its constitution, the Committee has held 29 meetings, with the latest meeting convened on 8 January 2026.

The reply further informed that proposals received from States and Union Territories are processed expeditiously. Clarifications sought from the Governments of Tamil Nadu, Kerala, Karnataka and Tripura have since been received, enabling further processing of their proposals under the Scheme.

With regard to Telangana, the Minister stated that the State Government has submitted its proposal for financial assistance for 2026-27, including assistance for providing incentives to inter-caste married couples where one spouse belongs to the Scheduled Caste community. He said in accordance with the Scheme guidelines, the Central Government has released ₹30.52 crores to the State.

The reply also informed that, to ensure uninterrupted implementation of the Scheme, the Ministry released a token amount of ₹128.4327 crores in April 2026 through Mother Sanction on the SNA-SPARSH platform, even before receiving proposals from the States and Union Territories. Subsequently, the second instalment of Central Assistance has also been released to eligible States and Union Territories whose proposals fulfilled the prescribed requirements.

The Government remains committed to ensuring effective implementation of the SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989 and the Protection of Civil Rights Act, 1955 by extending timely financial support, strengthening institutional monitoring and working closely with States and Union Territories to safeguard the rights, dignity and welfare of Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes.

item.title: Government Strengthens Monitoring of De-addiction Centres Through NMBA Management Information System
item.dc:creator: Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment
item.description: Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment Government Strengthens Monitoring of De-addiction Centres Through NMBA Management Information System Patient-centric digital monitoring and regular inspections ensure quality treatment and rehabilitation services under NAPDDR Posted On: 29 JUL 2026 6:35PM by PIB Delhi The Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment has strengthened the monitoring and evaluation of de-addiction and rehabilitation centres supported under the National Action Plan for Drug Demand Reduction (NAPDDR) through a robust digital monitoring mechanism and…
item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment
Government Strengthens Monitoring of De-addiction Centres Through NMBA Management Information System
Patient-centric digital monitoring and regular inspections ensure quality treatment and rehabilitation services under NAPDDR
Posted On: 29 JUL 2026 6:35PM by PIB Delhi

The Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment has strengthened the monitoring and evaluation of de-addiction and rehabilitation centres supported under the National Action Plan for Drug Demand Reduction (NAPDDR) through a robust digital monitoring mechanism and periodic inspections. This was stated by Minister of State for Social Justice and Empowerment, Shri B. L. Verma, in a written reply to Shri Karti P Chidambaram in the Lok Sabha.

The Ministry stated that the performance of de-addiction and rehabilitation centres is assessed on a comprehensive set of parameters. These include adequacy of infrastructure such as bed capacity and occupancy, ward space, counselling and consultation rooms, medicine storage, recreation facilities, cleanliness, and provision of free food. Assessments also examine staffing, quality of medical and psychosocial services, follow-up care, maintenance of records, utilization of funds, and outreach activities undertaken by the centres.

To further improve service delivery, the Ministry has introduced the Nasha Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan Management Information System (NMBA MIS) under NAPDDR. The digital platform captures and monitors beneficiary-wise records from preventive, treatment and rehabilitation facilities across the country. It records patient registration details, clinical assessments, substance use patterns, diagnosis, treatment, pharmacological and psychosocial interventions, and follow-up services. The system enables effective monitoring of treatment outcomes and rehabilitation of beneficiaries.

The Ministry also informed that de-addiction centres are regularly inspected by the Project Monitoring Unit through random surprise visits in accordance with the Standard Operating Procedure. Continuation of projects and release of grants are contingent upon satisfactory inspection reports. Centres found not functioning in accordance with the Scheme guidelines are liable for closure, ensuring accountability and quality standards in service delivery.

The Government remains committed to strengthening India's de-addiction ecosystem through transparent monitoring, digital governance, and quality rehabilitation services, contributing to the objectives of a healthier and drug-free society.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment
Government Expands Welfare and Empowerment Initiatives for SCs, OBCs, Senior Citizens and Persons with Disabilities in Tamil Nadu
Nearly 9.67 Lakh SC Students Receive Post-Matric Scholarships in 2025-26; Over 8.75 Lakh OBC Students Covered Under Pre-Matric Scholarship in 2024-25
Posted On: 29 JUL 2026 6:34PM by PIB Delhi

The Government of India continues to strengthen educational, economic and social empowerment of Scheduled Castes (SCs), Other Backward Classes (OBCs), Senior Citizens and Persons with Disabilities (PwDs) in Tamil Nadu through a wide range of flagship schemes implemented by the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment. This information was given by Minister of State for Social Justice and Empowerment Shri Ramdas Athawale in a written reply in the Rajya Sabha.

The Minister informed that under the Post-Matric Scholarship for Scheduled Castes, the number of beneficiaries increased from 6,43,761 in 2023-24 to 9,34,793 in 2024-25 and further to 9,66,840 in 2025-26. Similarly, the Pre-Matric Scholarship for SCs and Others benefited 3,35,642 students in 2023-24, 5,21,124 students in 2024-25 and 5,82,684 students in 2025-26.

Under the Pradhan Mantri Anusuchit Jaati Abhyuday Yojana (PM-AJAY), the number of beneficiaries increased from 507 in 2023-24 to 894 in 2024-25, while 666 beneficiaries were covered during 2025-26.

The SRESHTA scheme for residential education benefited 238 students in 2023-24, 312 students in 2024-25 and 267 students in 2025-26.

The reply further stated that the Ministry continued to support students belonging to OBCs, Economically Backward Classes (EBCs) and Denotified, Nomadic and Semi-Nomadic Tribes (DNTs). Under the Pre-Matric Scholarship Scheme, 2.94 lakh students in 2023-24, 8.75 lakh students in 2024-25 and 2.76 lakh students have been benefitted in 2025-26. The Post-Matric Scholarship Scheme covered 4.76 lakh, 4.59 lakh and 3.67 lakh students, respectively.

The reply said that the beneficiaries under the Top Class Education Scheme in Schools increased significantly from 725 in 2023-24 to 10,735 in 2025-26, while the National Fellowship for OBC Students supported 78 scholars in 2023-24, 92 in 2024-25 and 116 in 2025-26.

The Minister further informed that welfare initiatives for senior citizens and economically weaker sections continued to benefit thousands of people in the State. Under the Integrated Programme for Senior Citizens (IPSrC) component of Atal Vayo Abhyuday Yojana (AVYAY), 32,940 senior citizens in 2023-24, 33,715 in 2024-25 and 24,390 senior citizens were covered in 2025-26. The lending schemes of the National Backward Classes Finance and Development Corporation (NBCFDC) benefited 20,618 persons in 2023-24, 18,377 persons in 2024-25 and 21,437 persons in 2025-26. Under the National Scheduled Castes Finance and Development Corporation (NSFDC), Income Generating Schemes supported 14,548 beneficiaries in 2023-24, 5,314 beneficiaries in 2024-25 and 8,085 beneficiaries in 2025-26. The National Fellowship for Scheduled Caste Students benefited 107 scholars, 102 scholars and 112 scholars, respectively, while the VISVAS scheme covered 5,092 beneficiaries in 2024-25 and 7,475 beneficiaries in 2025-26.

The reply also informed that under the Centrally Sponsored Scheme for implementation of the Protection of Civil Rights Act, 1955 and the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989, relief was provided to 5,586 atrocity victims in both 2023-24 and 2024-25, while 6,042 victims received relief during 2025-26. The financial incentives were extended to 2,392 inter-caste marriage couples in 2023-24, 2,476 couples in 2024-25 and 2,202 couples in 2025-26.

The Deendayal Divyangjan Rehabilitation Scheme (DDRS) benefited 1,052 persons in 2023-24, 1,036 persons in 2024-25 and 878 persons in 2025-26, respectively, while the Scholarship Scheme for Students with Disabilities supported 4,046 students in 2023-24, 3,851 students in 2024-25 and 4,043 students in 2025-26.

The Minister further stated that welfare of Scheduled Castes is undertaken through 38 Ministries under the Development Action Plan for Scheduled Castes (DAPSC).

An assessment carried out by the Development Monitoring and Evaluation Office (DMEO), NITI Aayog has observed that the Ministry's targeted interventions have contributed to notable improvements in access to education for marginalized communities. The Government remains committed to ensuring inclusive and equitable development by strengthening educational opportunities, livelihood support, financial inclusion and social protection for all vulnerable sections of society.

The scheme is aligned with NEP 2020 to ensure that all children have access to quality education with an equitable and inclusive classroom environment which should take care of their diverse background, multilingual needs, different academic abilities and make them active participants in the…
item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Education
Access to Quality Education
Posted On: 29 JUL 2026 6:32PM by PIB Delhi

The Department of School Education & Literacy is implementing an integrated scheme  for school education - Samagra Shiksha, which covers the entire gamut from pre-school to class  XII. The scheme is aligned with NEP 2020 to ensure that all children have access to quality  education with an equitable and inclusive classroom environment which should take care of  their diverse background, multilingual needs, different academic abilities and make them active  participants in the learning process. 

Under the scheme, financial assistance is provided to States and UTs for undertaking  various activities for providing universal access to holistic and qualitative school education  including opening/strengthening of new schools up to senior secondary level, construction of  school buildings & additional classrooms, development/strengthening of school infrastructure  in border areas under Vibrant Village Programme through the convergence of existing scheme of DOSEL, setting up, construction of hostels for PVTGs under PM-JANMAN, setting up of  Netaji Subhash Chandra Bose Avasiya Vidyalayas, construction of hostels under Dharti Aaba  Janjatiya Gram Utkarsh Abhiyan for unsaturated ST population, free uniforms to eligible  children and free text books at elementary level, transport allowance and undertaking enrolment & retention drives. Special training for age-appropriate admission of out of school children and residential as well as non-residential training for older children, seasonal hostels / residential  camps, special training centers at worksites, transport/ escort facility etc. are also supported to bring out of school children to the formal schooling system. Support is also provided for skill  education, integrated science labs/maths. 

PM eVidya unifies all efforts related to digital/online/on-air education to enable multi-mode access to education across the country under the aegis of National Education Policy (NEP)  2020. PM eVidya includes 200 DTH TV Channels and 400 Radio channels to provide  supplementary education as per requirement in various Indian languages for classes 1-12. 

Pradhan Mantri Schools for Rising India (PM SHRI) is a centrally sponsored scheme which aims to strengthen more than 14,500 schools from amongst the existing schools managed by Central Government/State/UT Government/local bodies. These PM SHRI schools are to showcase all the initiatives of National Education Policy (NEP) 2020, be exemplar schools, and also offer benchmarking leadership to other schools in the neighbourhood. 

Under the Scheme(s), annual plans are prepared by the respective States /UTs, including  for rural and underserved areas, as per their priority and requirements. These annual plans are  appraised and approved by the Project Approval Board (PAB) in the Department, in  consultation with the respective State/UT, as per the programmatic and financial norms of the Scheme. 

Accordingly, for 2026-27, under Samagra Shiksha, central share of Rs 722.93 crore has been approved for the State of Punjab and under PM SHRI, central share of Rs 140.10 crore for 356 PM SHRI Schools has been approved for the State of Punjab for providing qualitative and  holistic education in the State. 

Further, education is in the concurrent list of the Constitution and the majority of the schools  are under the administrative control of the respective State/UT Government. 

Inclusive Education component of Samagra Shiksha provides support to CwSN via  specific student-oriented interventions such as identification and assessment camps, provision of aids, appliances and assistive devices, scribe, transportation and escort allowance support, Braille books and large print books, stipend for girls with special needs and teaching-learning  materials etc. in order to appropriately address their unique educational requirements in general schools. Further, individualized support is also provided through therapeutic interventions at  the block level. Samagra Shiksha also has provisions for creation of differently abled friendly  infrastructure such as ramps with handrails and differently-abled friendly toilets for barrier free  access in schools. 

The Government of India is implementing a Centrally Sponsored Scheme called Nav Bharat Saaksharta Karyakram, popularly known as ULLAS: Understanding of Lifelong Learning for All in Society from 2022-23 to 2026-27. The scheme, aligned with NEP 2020 targets adults (aged 15 and above) who are not literate and focuses on rural areas, districts/blocks with large SC/ST/ population, educationally backward areas, women etc. The  scheme is implemented in a hybrid mode, allowing States/UTs to adopt offline, online or  blended approaches. The scheme is based on volunteerism to impart foundational literacy and numeracy. 9 States/ UTs (Ladakh, Mizoram, Tripura, Goa, Himachal Pradesh, A & N Islands, Chandigarh, Sikkim and Uttarakhand) have declared Full Literacy. 

The Central Government provides financial assistance to States/UTs under the Centrally Sponsored scheme - Samagra Shiksha for strengthening of existing government  schools, including, creation and augmentation of infrastructure facilities like buildings, toilets  for Boys/Girls/CWSN, drinking water, electricity and digital facilities based on Annual Work Plan & Budget (AWP&B) proposal prepared by them and gaps determined from Unified District Information System for Education (UDISE) database. These plans are then appraised and approved by the Project Approval Board (PAB) in the Department of School Education and Literacy in consultation with the State/UT as per the programmatic and financial norms of the scheme, physical and financial progress of works sanctioned earlier and availability of  budgetary resources. 

The Department of School Education & Literacy, from time to time, through review  meetings and PAB meetings, requests the State Governments and UT administrations to fill  up infrastructure gaps.

This information was given by Minister of State for Education, Shri Jayant Chaudhary, in a written reply in the Rajya Sabha today.

*****

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Education
Vacancies in Schools
Posted On: 29 JUL 2026 6:29PM by PIB Delhi

Education being a subject in the Concurrent List of the Constitution, the majority of  schools in the country are under the administrative control of the respective State Governments  and Union Territory Administrations. Accordingly, the recruitment, service conditions and  deployment of teachers fall within the administrative domain of the concerned States/UTs. Teacher vacancies arise from time to time due to factors such as retirement, resignation, creation of new posts, rationalisation of teacher deployment and changes in enrolment, including in rural, tribal and aspirational districts. The data relating to sanctioned strength, working strength and vacancies of teachers in Government schools at the primary, upper primary, secondary and senior secondary levels, State-wise, is maintained by the respective State Governments and Union Territory Administrations. 

As per the UDISE+ 2025-26, the State/UT-wise details of teachers in position in Government  schools across the country, are placed at Annexure-I. 

Further, as per the UDISE+ 2025-26, the State/UT-wise details of single-teacher schools in the  country, are placed at Annexure-II. 

The Central Government periodically advises States/UTs to fill vacant posts through transparent and merit-based recruitment processes, including through autonomous teacher recruitment boards or similar mechanisms. The progress of recruitment is regularly reviewed through meetings and advisories, with emphasis on competitive selection, consistency and  technology-based teacher requirement planning and forecasting.

Further, the Central Government provides financial assistance to States/UTs under Samagra  Shiksha to maintain appropriate Pupil-Teacher Ratio (PTR) at various levels of schooling in  accordance with the norms prescribed under the Right of Children to Free and Compulsory  Education (RTE) Act, 2009. 

Para 2.3 of the National Education Policy (NEP), 2020 emphasises maintaining a PTR of under  30:1 in each school and under 25:1 in areas with a high proportion of socio-economically  disadvantaged students. As per UDISE+ 2025-26 report, the PTR at the national level stands  at 19 at Primary level, 17 at Upper Primary level, 15 at Secondary level, and 23 at the Higher  Secondary level which is within the norms envisaged under NEP 2020. 

Moreover, the Ministry of Education is implementing a National Mission to improve learning  outcomes at the School Education level through an integrated teacher training programme  called ‘National Initiative for School Heads’ and Teachers’ Holistic Advancement’  (NISHTHA). NISHTHA courses have been designed and are run for Elementary, Secondary,  Foundational Literacy and Numeracy (FLN), Early Childhood Care and Education (ECCE)  and Educational Technology and are offered online by NCERT on the DIKSHA platform using high-quality professionally made e-content.

This information was given by Minister of State for Education, Shri Jayant Chaudhary, in a written reply in the Rajya Sabha today.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Education
National Education Policy (NEP), 2020
Posted On: 29 JUL 2026 6:26PM by PIB Delhi

In line with the recommendations of the National Education Policy (NEP), 2020, skill-based and experiential learning has been promoted across school and higher education. Under the Centrally Sponsored Scheme of Samagra Shiksha, skill education has been integrated as a regular component for students of Classes VI to XII. For Classes VI to VIII, exposure to skill education is provided through pre-vocational education, including 10 bagless days, a separate off-textbook experiential learning programme and Kaushal Bodh, the NCERT activity-based textbook series. For Classes IX to XII, skill courses aligned with the National Skills Qualifications Framework (NSQF) are offered, with skill modules as an additional subject at the Secondary level and skill courses as an elective subject at the Senior Secondary level.

In higher education, skill-based education is supported through Community Colleges, B.Voc. Degree Programmes and Deen Dayal Upadhyay Centres for Knowledge Acquisition and Upgradation of Skilled Human Abilities and Livelihood. Further, UGC and AICTE have issued Guidelines for Apprenticeship Embedded Degree Programme (AEDP), 2025 for higher education programmes under their respective domains. AEDP with National Apprenticeship Training Scheme (NATS), provides opportunities to combine academic learning with structured apprenticeship and on-the-job training and industry exposure. Skill-based learning is also supported through programmes in emerging areas such as Artificial Intelligence, Data Science, Cyber Security, Quantum Technology, Space Technology, Sustainable Energy, Internet of Things, Robotics and Semiconductors. These initiatives promote experiential, skill-based and industry-linked learning and support the development of employability and entrepreneurial abilities.

The Ministry of Education implements ICT and Digital initiatives such as PM eVidya and DIKSHA under Samagra Shiksha to enhance digital learning in Government schools across the country including the rural, remote and tribal areas. The initiatives aim to enhance the quality of education by integrating technology into teaching and learning processes. Under the scheme, funds are provided for setting up ICT Labs and Smart Classrooms according to the requirement of the State submitted in the Annual Work Plan & Budget (AWP&B).

A comprehensive initiative called PM eVidya was initiated as part of Atma Nirbhar Bharat Abhiyaan on 17th May, 2020, which unifies all efforts related to digital/online/on-air education to enable multi-mode access to education across the country. States/UTs collaborate with NCERT to utilise, monitor and evaluate the effectiveness of these initiatives as per their requirements. The key components of PM eVidya are also aligned towards enhancing digital literacy and include 200 DTH TV channels and 400 Radio channels to enable all States/UTs to provide supplementary education in various Indian languages for classes 1-12.

Digital Infrastructure for Knowledge Sharing (DIKSHA) is the Nation’s One Nation, One Digital platform for providing quality e-content for school education in States/UTs along with QR coded Energised Textbooks (ETBs) for all grades. As a participant in DIKSHA, States/UTs/Autonomous Bodies (ABs) have generated and contributed over 3.67 lakh content in mother tongue/local/regional languages enabling multilingualism. Overall, 579.41 crore learning sessions for 2.29 crore users have been completed on DIKSHA by students, teachers and other stakeholders. The stakeholders also have access to more than 836 Virtual Labs on DIKSHA that help them with simulation of real-world laboratory environments. The platform supports both online and offline access, enabling learners to download content and continue learning without internet connectivity. These digital initiatives provide free curriculum aligned e-content to students, parents and teachers for supplementary academic resources.

The Government of India, in the Budget 2025, has announced provision of broadband connectivity to all Government Secondary schools in rural areas, under the ‘BharatNet’ project by BSNL to enhance digital infrastructure in remote areas in a phased manner.

To bridge the urban-rural education divide, Samagra Shiksha focuses on equal opportunities for schooling, equitable learning outcomes, bridging social and gender gaps and ensuring equity and inclusion in school education. The availability of digital learning platforms, smart classrooms and other technology-enabled learning resources provides access to educational content across different regions.

In higher education, digital learning platforms such as SWAYAM, SWAYAM Prabha, e-PG Pathshala and the UGC e-resource portal provide access to educational content and courses. The integration of the UGC e-resource portal with the Digital Seva Portal enables access to digital learning resources through Common Service Centres, including in rural areas. The UGC e-resource portal also provides selected digital content in regional languages. Further, the regulatory framework for Open and Distance Learning and Online Education provides for access to higher education through these modes while the Malaviya Mission Teacher Training Programme includes faculty capacity-building through technology-enabled and ICT-based pedagogy. The Union Budget 2026–27 announced provision of Viability Gap Funding (VGF)/capital support for girls' hostels in Higher Education Science, Technology, Engineering and Mathematics (STEM) institutions, covering every district. There was also an announcement in Budget 2025-2026 of Bhartiya Bhasha Pustak Yojana (BBPY) to provide digital-form Indian language books for school and higher education. These measures support access to education and digital learning opportunities across different regions.

This information was given by the Minister of State for Education Dr Sukanta  Majumdar, in a written reply in Rajya Sabha today.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Education
Posts and Vacancies in Higher Education
Posted On: 29 JUL 2026 6:24PM by PIB Delhi

The Central Higher Education Institutions (CHEIs) under Ministry of Education  including Central Universities (CUs) and Centrally Funded Technical Institutions (CFTIs) such as  Indian Institutes of Technology (IITs), and National Institutes of Technology (NITs) are statutory  autonomous organizations established under respective Central Acts of Parliament and governed  by provisions of the Acts/Statutes/Ordinances/Regulations made thereunder. As autonomous  institutions, faculty recruitment is done within the institutions itself, in accordance with their Acts and Regulations. The recruitment powers vests with the respective Board of Governors/Executive  Committee/Board of Management. 

Occurring of vacancies and filling thereof is a continuous process. The vacancies arise due to  promotion, retirement, resignation, death, opening of new institutions, schemes or projects, and additional requirements on account of enhanced students’ strength and expansion of capacity in  existing institutions. 

In August, 2021, all CHEIs under the Ministry of Education were requested to undertake a special drive to fill backlog vacancies in their institutions in Mission Mode. The CHEIs undertook special  recruitment drives to fill the vacancies including Scheduled Castes (SCs), Scheduled Tribes (STs) and Other Backward Classes (OBCs). In September 2022, the Ministry of Education had also exhorted all the CHEIs to fill up the vacancies in Mission Mode. In October 2025, all the CHEIs have again been requested to fill up all the backlog vacancies in Mission Mode. From September 2022, all CHEIs have undertaken Mission Mode recruitment drive to fill the vacancies. Up to  23.05.2026 (i.e. the date of last Rozgar Mela), a total number of 32,114 posts (3,851 SC, 1,643 ST,  6,785 OBC, 1,191 EWS) have been filled up by all CHEIs, including 18,757 faculty positions (2,315  SC, 910 ST, 3,986 OBC, 568 EWS), in Mission Mode. 

The number of PhD admissions at CHEIs is dynamic and varies across admission cycles based  on the availability of faculty supervisors, departmental requirements, and funding support. Further,  the availability of PhD positions changes with the Institute’s faculty strength. New faculty members create additional research supervision capacity, while the research scholars of faculty members who resign, retire, or are transferred are reassigned to other eligible supervisors as per  the Institute’s academic regulations. The number of PhD enrolment has increased from 1,17,301  (as per AISHE Report 2014-15) to 3,43,559 (as per AISHE Report 2023-24) marking a growth of 192.89 %. 

This information was given by the Minister of State in the Ministry of Education, Dr. Sukanta Majumdar, in a written reply in Rajya Sabha today.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Education
CABE Meetings for Union–State Synergy in Education
Posted On: 29 JUL 2026 6:22PM by PIB Delhi

A special session of the Central Advisory Board of Education (CABE) was held on 21.09.2019 to deliberate on the Draft National Education Policy (NEP). NEP 2020 inter-alia envisages that its successful implementation requires a long-term vision, sustained expertise and coordinated efforts at the National, State, institutional and individual levels. Accordingly, the Policy recommends strengthening and empowering the CABE with an expanded mandate to serve as a platform for consultation and to develop, articulate, evaluate and review the vision of education, besides reviewing the institutional framework for achieving the objectives of NEP 2020.

In order to advise the Ministry of Education on critical aspects of implementation of NEP 2020 and also to facilitate the comprehensive, holistic, synergetic, and systematic implementation of the policy across school and higher education, the Ministry of Education has constituted an Education Advisory Council (EdAC) comprising eminent experts from diverse fields of education. The Council is to advise the Ministry on critical aspects of NEP implementation, facilitate its comprehensive, holistic and synergetic implementation across school and higher education, develop an overarching roadmap, review interventions for course correction, and recommend measures for strengthening the CABE.

The Government accords high importance to cooperative federalism and continuous & regular engagement with States and Union Territories on matters relating to education. Since the announcement of NEP, 2020, consultations with States/UTs, academia, industry and other stakeholders have been undertaken on a regular basis through various institutional forums to discuss and deliberate on issues related to education policies and educational reforms. These include the National Education Ministers' Conference (June 2022), the National Conference of Chief Secretaries (2022, 2023 and 2025), the 7th, 9th and 11th Governing Council Meetings of NITI Aayog (2022, 2024 and 2026 respectively), consultation-cum-review meetings with States/UTs (October and December 2022), zone-wise consultation-cum-review meetings (February, March, May and June 2023), a one-day national workshop and two regional workshops (November 2021), National Conference on Curricular and Assessment Equivalence and Improving Learning Outcomes (July 2025), Akhil Bharatiya Shiksha Samagam (2022, 2023, 2024 and 2025), the Conference of Governors (2021 and 2024), and the National Workshop on Higher and Technical Education with Secretaries of States/UTs (November 2024). Recently on 22-23 July 2026, a two-Day Conclave of State and UT Education Ministers was held in New Delhi where key policy leaders from across the country, inter-alia deliberated to review the implementation of major centrally sponsored schemes in School education, and to strengthen centre-state collaboration and knowledge sharing for better educational outcomes. These engagements provide a regular platform for collaborative policy formulation, review and implementation of educational reforms.

This information was given by the Minister of State in the Ministry of Education, Dr. Sukanta Majumdar, in a written reply in Rajya Sabha today.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Education
Teacher Vacancies
Posted On: 29 JUL 2026 6:19PM by PIB Delhi

Education being a subject in the Concurrent List of the Constitution, the majority of schools in the country are under the administrative control of the respective State Governments and Union Territory Administrations. Accordingly, the recruitment, service conditions and deployment of teachers fall within the administrative domain of the concerned States/UTs. Teacher vacancies arise from time to time due to factors such as retirement, resignation, creation of new posts, rationalisation of teacher deployment and changes in enrolment, including in rural, tribal and aspirational districts. Data relating to sanctioned teacher posts, teachers in position against sanctioned posts, teacher vacancies and the reasons for such vacancies in Government schools, State-wise, including in the States of Telangana and Andhra Pradesh, for the period from 2024 to 2026, are maintained by the respective State Governments and Union Territory Administrations.

As per UDISE+ 2025-26, the State/UT-wise details of teachers in position in schools across the country from 2023-24, 2024-25 and 2025-26 are placed at Annexure I.

Recruitment of teachers is a continuous process undertaken by the respective State Governments/UT Administrations in accordance with their recruitment rules and procedures. Vacancies arise from time to time due to factors such as retirement, resignation, creation of new posts consequent to enhanced student enrolment and establishment of new schools. The timeline for filling up such vacancies is also determined by the respective State Governments/UT Administrations.

The Central Government periodically advises States/UTs to fill vacant posts through transparent and merit-based recruitment processes, including through autonomous teacher recruitment boards or similar mechanisms. The progress of recruitment is regularly reviewed through meetings and advisories, with emphasis on competitive selection, consistency and technology-based teacher requirement planning and forecasting.

Further, the Central Government provides financial assistance to States/UTs under Samagra Shiksha to maintain appropriate Pupil-Teacher Ratio (PTR) at various levels of schooling in accordance with the norms prescribed under the Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education (RTE) Act, 2009.

Para 2.3 of the National Education Policy (NEP), 2020 emphasises maintaining a Pupil Teacher Ratio (PTR) of under 30:1 in each school and under 25:1 in areas with a high proportion of socio-economically disadvantaged students. As per UDISE+ 2025-26, the national PTR stands at 10 at the Foundational Stage, 12 at the Preparatory Stage, 17 at the Middle Stage and 21 at the Secondary Stage. In the State of Telangana, the corresponding PTR is 11, 10, 11 and 14, while in the State of Andhra Pradesh, it is 11, 12, 16 and 15, respectively, which are within the norms envisaged under NEP 2020.

Education is in the Concurrent list of the Constitution and the opening, merger/closing/consolidation/rationalisation of schools are within the purview of respective State Government and UT Administration-which are the appropriate Government under the Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education (RTE) Act, 2009.

As per UDISE+, the State/UT-wise number of Government schools from 2023-24, 2024-25 and 2025-26 are placed at Annexure II.

Under the integrated centrally sponsored scheme of Samagra Shiksha, financial assistance is provided to the States and UTs for opening/strengthening of new schools up to senior secondary level, construction of school buildings & additional classrooms.

This information was given by Minister of State for Education, Shri Jayant Chaudhary, in a written reply in Rajya Sabha today.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Rural Development
MoRD and PCI India Sign Non-Financial MoU to Strengthen Women-Led Enterprises through Public Procurement
Posted On: 29 JUL 2026 6:16PM by PIB Delhi

The Ministry of Rural Development (MoRD), through the Deendayal Antyodaya Yojana–National Rural Livelihoods Mission (DAY-NRLM), today signed a Non-Financial Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) with Project Concern International (PCI) India to strengthen women-led enterprises (WLEs), particularly Self-Help Group (SHG)-led enterprises, through public procurement and market-linked enterprise development.

The MoU signing ceremony was held under the chairpersonship of Shri Rohit Kansal, Secretary, Department of Rural Development. The MoU was signed and exchanged between Ms. Swati Sharma, Joint Secretary (Rural Livelihoods), Ministry of Rural Development, and Mr. Indrajit Chaudhuri, CEO & Country Director, PCI India.

The MoU formalises the collaboration initiated in 2022 under the initiative “Leveraging Public Procurement for Women’s Economic Empowerment”, supported by the Bill & Melinda Gates Foundation (BMGF). The partnership seeks to enhance the participation of women-led and SHG enterprises in government and institutional procurement through enterprise readiness, capacity building and market linkages.

The three-year MoU, covering 2026–2029, is non-financial in nature and involves no transfer of funds or financial obligation between the parties. Each party will bear its own costs for activities undertaken under the MoU.

A key component of the partnership is the proposed establishment of a National Resource Cell (NRC)/Public Procurement and Business Model Support Cell within DAY-NRLM, with technical support from PCI India. The Cell will provide strategic and operational support to strengthen procurement-linked enterprise ecosystems across SRLMs.

The partnership will support the development of enterprise incubation frameworks, SOPs, operational toolkits and standardised capacity-building modules. It will also facilitate training and handholding of SRLM teams and SHG enterprises on Government e-Marketplace (GeM) onboarding, tender participation, quality standards, documentation and procurement compliance. The collaboration will further explore and promote sustainable enterprise models through renewable energy integration, sustainable production practices and convergence with relevant government agencies.

During FY 2026–27, focused technical assistance is proposed initially in Assam, Bihar, Jharkhand, Karnataka, Maharashtra, Rajasthan and Uttar Pradesh, while enabling wider engagement with other States. National technical learning sessions, cross-State knowledge-sharing, enterprise opportunity mapping and development of scalable procurement-linked business models will also be undertaken.

The MoU marks an important step towards institutionalising technical support for enabling SHG enterprises to access public procurement markets, build sustainable and scalable businesses and advance women's economic empowerment. The partnership is aligned with the objectives of DAY-NRLM and the national vision of creating 6 crore Lakhpati Didis through sustainable, enterprise-led and market-linked livelihoods.

The collaboration also contributes to the broader national goals of Viksit Bharat 2047, the Sustainable Development Goals and India's Net Zero aspirations by promoting inclusive, sustainable and market-oriented livelihood opportunities for rural women.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Personnel, Public Grievances & Pensions
Lok Sabha Passes Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Amendment Bill, 2026
Dr. Jitendra Singh says amendments will further strengthen legal framework to curb examination malpractices and ensure speedy justice
Posted On: 29 JUL 2026 6:02PM by PIB Delhi

The Lok Sabha today passed the Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Amendment Bill, 2026 by a voice vote after an extensive discussion. Replying to the debate, Union Minister of State (Independent Charge) for Science & Technology; Earth Sciences and Minister of State in the Prime Minister's Office, Personnel, Public Grievances and Pensions, Atomic Energy and Space, Dr. Jitendra Singh said the amendments would further strengthen the legal framework to prevent unfair means in public examinations and safeguard the interests of students and youth.

Dr. Jitendra Singh said the Government remains committed to ensuring the integrity, transparency and credibility of the public examination system. He said the amendments reflect the Government's openness to incorporate constructive inputs, learn from experience and further strengthen the law in order to effectively tackle organised examination-related crimes.

The Minister noted that the Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Act, 2024 was enacted to provide a comprehensive legal framework to curb unfair means in public examinations conducted by major recruitment agencies, including the Union Public Service Commission (UPSC), Staff Selection Commission (SSC), Railway Recruitment Boards (RRBs), Institute of Banking Personnel Selection (IBPS) and the National Testing Agency (NTA) for higher education admissions. He said the Act had already made offences under its ambit cognizable, non-bailable and non-compoundable with stringent penal provisions.

Highlighting the key provisions of the Amendment Bill, Dr. Jitendra Singh said the punishment for persons resorting to unfair means has been enhanced from imprisonment of three to five years to five to ten years, while the maximum fine has been increased from ₹10 lakh to ₹50 lakh. For service providers involved in such offences, the maximum fine has been enhanced from ₹1 crore to ₹5 crore and the period of debarment from conducting public examinations has been increased from four years to eight years. Punishment for directors and senior management of service providers has also been enhanced from three to ten years' imprisonment to five to ten years, with the maximum fine increased from ₹1 crore to ₹5 crore. The Bill further enhances punishment for organised crime from five to ten years' imprisonment to seven to ten years and increases the maximum fine from ₹1 crore to ₹10 crore.

The Minister said the Amendment Bill provides for the establishment of Special Fast Track Courts for offences relating to public examinations and envisages completion of investigation within two months and completion of trial within three months from the date of filing of the charge sheet. The Bill also provides for appointment of Special Public Prosecutors and empowers the Government to constitute a Special Task Force for investigation of offences under the Act, thereby ensuring swift and effective action against organised examination-related crimes. He also referred to the Prime Minister's announcement of a high-level task force comprising eminent experts to make the public examination system "leak-proof" and said substantial progress has been made in implementing the recommendations aimed at strengthening the examination ecosystem.

Referring to the implementation of the 2024 Act, the Minister said that 52 FIRs have already been registered under its provisions, demonstrating the Government's commitment to strict enforcement and prompt action against examination-related offences. He said the objective of the amendments is to ensure that honest and deserving students are rewarded for their genuine efforts while organised examination-related crimes are dealt with through stringent legal provisions and speedy justice.

Concluding the discussion, Dr. Jitendra Singh said the passage of the Amendment Bill marks another significant step towards reinforcing public confidence in the fairness, transparency and credibility of the country's public examination system while safeguarding the aspirations of millions of students and job aspirants.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Defence
LAUNCH OF MACHILIPATNAM, THE SEVENTH OF THE MAHE-CLASS ANTI-SUBMARINE WARFARE SHALLOW WATER CRAFT
Posted On: 29 JUL 2026 5:56PM by PIB Delhi

Machilipatnam (BY 529), the seventh of eight Anti-Submarine Warfare Shallow Water Craft (ASW SWC), being built by Cochin Shipyard Limited (CSL) for the Indian Navy, was launched on 29 Jul 2026 by Mrs Goolrukh Anand in the presence of Vice Admiral Atul Anand, Additional Secretary of Department of Military Affairs. The ceremony was attended by senior officials of the Indian Navy, Cochin Shipyard Limited, and other distinguished guests.

Machilipatnam carries deep historical and cultural significance as it derives its name from the historic port city of Machilipatnam, in Krishna district of Andhra Pradesh, known for its rich maritime legacy and flourishing trade along India's eastern seaboard. The ship proudly embodies the spirit and legacy of Machilipatnam while reinforcing the Indian Navy's commitment to safeguarding the nation's maritime interests.

The ship is equipped for Underwater Surveillance, Anti-Submarine Warfare (ASW) operations, and Low Intensity Maritime Operations (LIMO), along with Mine Warfare capability. The ship will further bolster coastal defence and enhance Maritime Domain Awareness.

The launch of Machilipatnam marks another milestone in the successful execution of the ASW SWC project and reaffirms India's commitment to Aatmanirbhar Bharat in defence manufacturing. With indigenous content exceeding 80 percent, the project showcases the growing capability of the Indian shipbuilding industry and will substantially enhance the Indian Navy's operational readiness for safeguarding the nation's maritime interests in the Indian Ocean Region.

Ministry of Road Transport & Highways
DEVELOPMENT OF HIGHWAYS IN ASPIRATIONAL DISTRICTS AND BORDER AREAS
Posted On: 29 JUL 2026 5:51PM by PIB Delhi

All the aspirational districts are connected with the National Highway (NH) network. State / Union Territory (UT) – wise details of completed NHs length during the last five years for NHs connecting aspirational districts are at Annexure-I.

NHs projects in 3,318 km length have been awarded during the last five years for improving connectivity in border areas, out of which 1,301 km has been constructed. State / UT – wise details of such projects are at Annexure-II.

State / UT – wise details of expenditure incurred towards development and maintenance of NHs,     including NHs providing connectivity to aspirational districts and border areas, during each of the last five years are at Annexure-III.

Development and maintenance of NHs is a continuous process. Works on all NHs, including development / capacity augmentation works on NHs providing connectivity to remote and strategically important areas, are accordingly taken up based on traffic density, connectivity requirement, condition of the road and synergy with PM Gati Shakti National Master Plan (NMP). At present, 1,191 NHs projects in about 25,917 km length costing ₹7.15 Lakh Crore are under construction in the country. This also includes development works in 3,100 km in border areas. Additionally, the Government has also taken up development of network of ropeways for improvement of first and last mile connectivity, accessibility, public convenience in remote areas.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Road Transport & Highways
GREEN HIGHWAY PROJECTS
Posted On: 29 JUL 2026 5:48PM by PIB Delhi

As part of the Green Highways (Plantation, Transplantation, Beautification and Maintenance) Policy 2015, Government undertakes plantation along available surplus median and roadside land of Right of Way (ROW) of various National Highway (NH) stretches in the country either as part of NHs projects or standalone basis, in accordance with Indian Roads Congress (IRC):SP:21 guidelines. During the last five years, approximately 1.32 Lakh km of NHs in the country have been covered with the plantation of over 3.61 Crore saplings.

State / Union Territory (UT) – wise details of plantation carried out along NHs during the last five years are at Annexure.

The cost of plantation and environmental mitigation activities is generally inbuilt into the total project cost of the respective NHs projects and expenditure is met from the overall funds allocated State / UT / Agency – wise for development and maintenance of NHs. Also, whenever

plantation work taken up on standalone basis, it is met out of overall fund allocated for NHs works.

Government has taken various policy reforms and initiatives to promote the adoption of recycled materials, waste products and environment friendly technologies in the construction and maintenance of NH projects. The policy framework encourages sustainable construction practices and promotes the potential use of recycled and waste-derived materials in projects wherever technically feasible. Continuous efforts through guidelines, advisories and technological advancements have created an enabling environment for wider adoption, thereby enhancing the potential and acceptance of recycled materials in construction activities.

Various sustainable and recycled materials, such as use of Bamboo Crash Barrier, use of Fly Ash / Pond Ash in embankment and structural works, Reclaimed Asphalt Pavement (RAP) in bituminous layers, and Construction and Demolition (C&D) Waste / Recycled Aggregates are utilized and used in suitable highway works as per technical specifications. The use of plastic waste in bituminous mixes, natural geo-textiles (such as Jute/ Coir etc.) in addition to other sustainable materials including Slag, Bio Bitumen / Molasses, Crumb Rubber, utilization of STP (Sewage Treatment Plant) treated water in road construction works and other recycled or industrial by-products are promoted as per feasibility and guidelines to improve pavement performance for addressing environmental concerns.

Further, Tree plantation and carbon offsetting measures have been integrated into NH projects as part of environmentally sustainable development. Plantation works are invariably taken up along with NHs projects or as separate drives also. Miyawaki plantation and drone monitoring of plantation has also been started to increase the green cover along NHs. Additionally, wherever tree felling is necessary for highway development, compensatory afforestation and tree transplantation are undertaken.

The adoption of green initiative practices, energy efficient construction technologies, digital monitoring systems, and improved environmental management practices have helped reduce emissions, conserve natural resources and minimize environmental impact during road construction.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Tribal Affairs
Ministry of Tribal Affairs Signed MoU with CSIR-NBRI for Conservation of Rare, Endangered, & Threatened (RET) Medicinal Plant Species, and to Safeguard Traditional Knowledge Empowering Tribal Communities
Posted On: 29 JUL 2026 5:20PM by PIB Delhi

In a major initiative to drive tribal welfare, foster sustainable livelihoods, and preserve traditional knowledge, the Ministry of Tribal Affairs (MoTA), Government of India, has signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) with the CSIR-National Botanical Research Institute (CSIR-NBRI), Lucknow. The primary objective of this three-year partnership is to establish a sustained, synergetic linkage between the two organizations to promote research and development for the conservation and ethnobotanical assessment of tribal bioresources across India.

The MoU was signed by Shri Manish Thakur, Additional Secretary, Ministry of Tribal Affairs, and Dr. Ajit Kumar Shasany, Director, CSIR, in the presence of Smt. Ranjana Chopra, Secretary, Ministry of Tribal Affairs. The occasion was also attended by Dr. Sharad Srivastava, Chief Scientist, CSIR, Dr. Sachitra Ratha, Scientist, CSIR, Dr. Manish Bhoyar, Scientist, CSIR, along with senior officials from the Ministry of Tribal Affairs.

Centering Tribal Welfare in Scientific Research

Under this agreement, tribal welfare and community sovereignty serve as the foundational principles for all scientific activities. The partnership focuses heavily on the conservation of Rare, Endangered, and Threatened (RET) medicinal plant species through advanced interventions, including the development of tissue culture facilities and specialized seed banks. To ensure long-term, community-managed sustainability, local tribal youth will receive hands-on capacity building and technical training in these propagation and conservation techniques. Furthermore, all field assessments and research activities will strictly require the Prior Informed Consent (PIC) of local Gram Sabhas and tribal communities, fully complying with the Biological Diversity Act, 2002. Every joint project proposal will feature a dedicated budget line item for grassroots community development, local value addition, and capacity building. To protect local interests, any intellectual property generated will be jointly owned by MoTA and CSIR-NBRI, held in trust for, or shared equitably with, contributing tribal communities, with financial gains funneled back through National or State Biodiversity Funds and dedicated MoTA welfare schemes. The agreement explicitly recognizes Traditional Knowledge as the intangible cultural heritage of tribal peoples, requiring strict compliance with national Access and Benefit Sharing mechanisms to prevent unauthorized commercialization.

Bridging Traditional Knowledge and Modern Science

Through joint thematic events, seminars, and sustained exchange programs involving traditional practitioners and scientists, MoTA aims to bridge tribal community knowledge with cutting-edge botanical science. By empowering tribal youth and strengthening local capacity, the alliance ensures that bioresource conservation directly translates into sustainable community development and cultural preservation.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Coal
COAL EXCHANGE RULES
Posted On: 29 JUL 2026 5:19PM by PIB Delhi

The Coal Exchange Rules, 2026, notified under Section 18B of the Mines and Minerals (Development and Regulation) Act, 1957 by the Ministry of Coal on 04.06.2026, establish a comprehensive regulatory framework to promote transparent and efficient trading of coal or lignite and its processed forms.

The salient features of the Coal Exchange Rules, 2026 are as follows:

  1. The Coal Controller Organisation (CCO) is the Authority to register and regulate Coal Exchange(s) in accordance with the eligibility criteria, procedure for registration, fees and charges, net worth, ownership structure and governance structure prescribed inter-alia in the Coal Exchange Rules, 2026. The Authority may specify operating procedures and issue guidelines, in consultation with the Central Government.
  2. Coal Exchange has been defined as an online platform, where buyers and sellers of coal and its processed forms, transact, trade and enter into contracts on such platform.
  3. The Authority shall evaluate, grant, renew and revoke exchange registrations, as well as approve exit schemes at the time of registration.
  4. The Authority shall exercise administrative control by approving the bidding and price discovery mechanisms, contract specifications regarding scheduling and delivery of transactions, quality of delivered coal, bid types, transaction fee ceilings, bye-laws and operating procedures.
  5. The Authority shall maintain market oversight to detect and prevent market manipulation, cartelization, insider trading, and abuse of dominant position. The Authority has been given power of intervention, power to issue interim orders and power of inspection in the event of any violation or non-compliance of any provisions of the rules.
  6. The Coal Exchange shall be established and operated with the objectives of formulating coal supply contracts, facilitating transactions of such contracts, ensuring fair, transparent, neutral, efficient, robust price discovery and dissemination, securing the efficient and timely supply of coal, in accordance with the terms of the contract. The Coal Exchange shall operate an electronic trading system and utlilise network communication for its operations.
  7. The Coal Exchange would operate a Settlement Guarantee Fund (SGF) managed by an independent committee, with at least 50% invested in safe/liquid instruments fixed deposits with the Scheduled public sector banks, treasury bills and Government securities.
  8. Coal Exchanges will have a market surveillance committee and a surveillance department to carry out day-to-day monitoring and surveillance of transactions, maintain an automated audit trail for bids, execute security audit of Information Technology Systems, maintenance of a disaster recovery site and alternate trading facility to ensure business continuity in the event of an emergency.
  9. The Coal Exchange will have a grievance redressal forum. The Authority may call for information from the Coal Exchange regarding the redressal of any specific grievance.

The estimated timeline for operationalisation of regulated coal exchange is 12 months from the date of receipt of an application, for registration of Coal exchange, on dedicated online application platform opened on 15.07.2026.

Any entity, including captive and commercial miners, consumers including small and medium consumers in the non-regulated sector can transact, trade and enter into delivery-based contracts on the Coal Exchange(s). The price discovery of the coal traded or transacted on the Coal Exchange shall be undertaken by the Coal Exchange through a mechanism that ensures fair, neutral, competitive and efficient prices. The bidding and price discovery mechanisms shall be conducted in accordance with the procedure approved by the Authority. The final price of the traded coal shall be adjusted in accordance with the quality of the coal traded, based on the price-adjustment mechanism of the contract executed and the quality certification issued by the coal sampling agency. The market oversight mechanism and market surveillance as envisioned in the 'Coal Exchange Rules, 2026' will prevent any market manipulation/abuse to bring transparency in the Coal Exchange ecosystem. Public Sector coal companies and small and medium consumers in the non-regulated sector may also leverage this platform to enhance market participation.

This information was given by Union Minister of State for Coal and Mines Shri Satish Chandra Dubey in a written reply in Lok Sabha today.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Chemicals and Fertilizers :
Department of Pharmaceuticals
Union Minister J. P. Nadda to address India Medical Device 2026
9th edition of flagship Conference to be held on 7th & 8th August, 2026 at New Delhi
Policymakers, Regulators, CEOs and MedTech leaders to deliberate on building a globally competitive medical devices ecosystem aligned with the vision of Viksit Bharat
Posted On: 29 JUL 2026 5:18PM by PIB Delhi

The Department of Pharmaceuticals, Ministry of Chemicals & Fertilizers, Government of India in collaboration with the Federation of Indian Chambers of Commerce & Industry (FICCI), is set to organise the 9th edition of India Medical Device 2026 on 7th and 8th August, 2026, at Vigyan Bhawan, New Delhi. The flagship event, themed "Towards Viksit Bharat: Advancing India as a Global Hub for Quality Medical Devices" will bring together policymakers, regulators, industry leaders, healthcare institutions, academia, innovators and global stakeholders to deliberate on the future roadmap of India's rapidly expanding medical devices and MedTech sector.

Union Minister of Chemical and Fertilizers, Shri Jagat Prakash Nadda, will address the event on "Atmanirbhar MedTech: Accelerating India's Journey towards Viksit Bharat" on 8 August 2026, outlining the Government's vision for building a globally competitive and innovation-driven medical devices ecosystem. Union Minister of State for Chemicals and Fertilizers, Smt. Anupriya Patel, will also address the Conference. Shri Manoj Joshi, Secretary, Department of Pharmaceuticals, Smt. Punya Salila Srivastava, Secretary, Ministry of Health & Family Welfare, Dr. Rajeev Singh Raghuvanshi, Drugs Controller General of India (DCGI), Dr. M. Srinivas, Member (Health), NITI Aayog, senior government officials, policymakers, CEOs of leading medical device companies, industry experts, start-ups and representatives from healthcare institutions and academia will participate in the two-day conference.

India Medical Device 2026 will feature high-level deliberations on key issues shaping the future of the sector, including localisation of medical device component manufacturing, strengthening testing infrastructure and quality assurance, building technology leadership in high-impact and high-volume medical devices, leveraging Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Software as a Medical Device (SaMD), enhancing clinical evidence generation and regulatory pathways, expanding India's medical device exports, strengthening service and maintenance ecosystems, and exploring reimbursement frameworks for innovative therapies in support of Universal Health Coverage (UHC).

India's medical devices industry, currently valued at over USD 15 billion, has emerged as one of the fastest-growing segments of the healthcare sector. The industry's growth has been supported by several transformative policy initiatives, including the National Medical Devices Policy 2023, Production Linked Incentive (PLI) Scheme, development of Medical Device Parks, strengthening of regulatory frameworks and sustained focus on research, innovation and quality manufacturing.

India Medical Device 2026 aims to further strengthen India's position as a global MedTech destination by fostering meaningful dialogue and partnerships across the medical devices value chain. The conference aims to promote investment, technology collaborations, innovation and adoption of global best practices while showcasing emerging technologies and start-up innovations that can accelerate the growth of India's medical devices ecosystem.

The event will witness participation from leading domestic and international stakeholders, reaffirming India's commitment to building an innovation-led, self-reliant and globally competitive medical devices sector aligned with the vision of Viksit Bharat@2047.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Heavy Industries
Ministry of Heavy Industries Extends Bid Submission Timeline for Global Tender under Scheme to Promote Manufacturing of Sintered Rare Earth Permanent Magnet (REPM scheme)
Posted On: 29 JUL 2026 5:16PM by PIB Delhi

The Ministry of Heavy Industries (MHI), Government of India, has extended timelines for global tender under the REPM scheme. The Bid Due Date has been extended from 29.07.2026 to 12.08.2026, while the opening of Technical Bids has been rescheduled from 30.07.2026 to 13.08.2026 to facilitate wider participation and provide additional time for stakeholders in the bidding process. The Addendum has been published on the Central Public Procurement (CPP) Portal for information of all stakeholders. (https://eprocure.gov.in/eprocure/app).

The global tender was invited by the Ministry on 20th March 2026 for selection of manufacturers as beneficiaries under REPM scheme to establish integrated rare earth permanent magnet manufacturing facilities in India.

On 26th November 2025, the Union Cabinet chaired by Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi approved the Scheme to Promote Manufacturing of Sintered Rare Earth Permanent Magnet with a financial outlay of Rs. 7,280 Crore. The Scheme, a first-of-its-kind initiative, aims to establish a total capacity of 6,000 Metric Tons Per Annum (MTPA) of integrated Rare Earth Permanent Magnet manufacturing facilities in India, thereby enhancing self-reliance and positioning India as a key player in the global REPM market.

Rare Earth Permanent Magnets are among the most powerful magnets in the world and are widely used in electric vehicles, wind turbines, high-end electronics, aerospace and defence systems. By building a complete value chain from NdPr oxide to finished magnets in India, the Scheme is expected to significantly reduce import dependence in this sector.

While significant steps have been taken to reduce emissions from passenger vehicles,…
item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Road Transport & Highways
Driving the Transition to Cleaner Mobility: PARIVARTAN Scheme for Modernizing Trucks and Buses in Delhi-NCR
A comprehensive initiative to replace ageing commercial vehicles with cleaner alternatives through targeted incentives and coordinated implementation
Posted On: 29 JUL 2026 5:07PM by PIB Delhi

For decades, deteriorating air quality has remained one of the most pressing environmental challenges in the Delhi-National Capital Region (NCR). While significant steps have been taken to reduce emissions from passenger vehicles, ageing commercial vehicles, especially trucks and buses, continue to contribute substantially to particulate matter (PM), nitrogen oxides (NOx), and other pollutants. With rising freight demand and rapid urbanization, modernizing the commercial vehicle fleet has emerged as a critical priority for improving air quality and public health.

To address this challenge, the Government of India approved a vehicle fleet renewal initiative to replace old and high-emission trucks and buses in Delhi-NCR with cleaner Bharat Stage (BS)-VI compliant and electric vehicles (EVs). Approved by the Union Cabinet on 3 June 2026, the initiative aims to accelerate the transition towards cleaner mobility through financial incentives, policy support, and coordinated implementation.

The initiative was subsequently named PARIVARTAN - Programme for Accelerated Renewal and Incentivization of Vehicle Assets for Reducing Transport Air Pollution and Network Emissions - reflecting the Government of India’s commitment to advancing sustainable transportation and improving air quality in the region through cleaner and more efficient vehicle technologies.

A Comprehensive Programme for Cleaner Transport

The PARIVARTAN Scheme has a total financial outlay of ₹9,585 crore, including ₹5,041 crore as Central Government support. The Ministry of Road Transport and Highways (MoRTH) will implement the scheme, while funding will be routed through the National Capital Region Planning Board (NCRPB) under the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs (MoHUA).

The programme covers the National Capital Territory of Delhi and the NCR districts of Haryana, Rajasthan and Uttar Pradesh, ensuring a coordinated regional approach to reducing vehicular pollution. Detailed operational guidelines have also been approved to ensure transparent and efficient implementation.

Replacing the Most Polluting Vehicles

The scheme targets commercial trucks and buses registered in Delhi-NCR that comply with BS-IV or older emission norms, including Pre-BS, BS-I, BS-II and BS-III vehicles.

More than 1.9 lakh trucks and over 16,000 buses are expected to become eligible under the programme, making it one of the country's most extensive commercial vehicle modernisation initiatives.

By encouraging owners to retire ageing vehicles and replace them with cleaner alternatives, the scheme seeks to significantly reduce transport-related emissions while promoting safer, more fuel-efficient technologies.

A Strong Package of Financial Incentives

To make vehicle replacement financially viable, the scheme offers a comprehensive package of incentives for eligible beneficiaries purchasing new BS-VI-compliant diesel/CNG vehicles or electric vehicles.

The benefits include:

  • 100% concession on Motor Vehicle Tax
  • 100% waiver on registration fees
  • 5% interest subvention on vehicle loans
  • Up to 8% discount offered by participating Original Equipment Manufacturers (OEMs)
  • Monthly fuel vouchers for BS-VI diesel and CNG vehicles
  • Equivalent one-time financial incentive for electric vehicles

Owners purchasing eligible used BS-VI vehicles will also receive financial support through tax concessions, interest subvention and fuel-related incentives, making cleaner technology accessible at lower acquisition costs.

Encouraging the Shift to Electric Mobility

The scheme provides additional support to accelerate the adoption of zero-emission vehicles.

Owners purchasing electric commercial vehicles will receive a one-time incentive equivalent to the discounted value of future fuel vouchers, substantially reducing the upfront cost of EV ownership.

For BS-VI diesel and CNG vehicles, beneficiaries will receive monthly fuel vouchers ranging from ₹1,200 to ₹4,800, depending on vehicle category, for a period of five years.

Electric vehicle buyers, in contrast, will receive a one-time incentive ranging from ₹64,000 to ₹2.56 lakh, providing immediate financial support while encouraging a faster transition to clean mobility.

Flexible Options for Vehicle Owners

Recognising the diverse operational and financial circumstances of commercial vehicle owners, the scheme provides multiple pathways for participation.

Eligible owners may:

  • Scrap their old vehicle at a Registered Vehicle Scrapping Facility (RVSF) and avail the applicable incentives.
  • Sell eligible BS-IV vehicles outside the NCR in designated non-National Clean Air Programme (NCAP) cities.
  • Trade the Certificate of Deposit (CD) if they choose not to purchase a replacement vehicle.

These flexible options ensure that beneficiaries can adopt the solution best suited to their business requirements while supporting the broader objective of reducing vehicular pollution.

Region-Specific Approach to Cleaner Mobility

The scheme incorporates region-specific provisions to maximise environmental benefits.

In Delhi, all replacement Light Goods Vehicles (LGVs) under the scheme must be electric, reinforcing the city's commitment to zero-emission urban freight transport.

In Haryana, Uttar Pradesh and Rajasthan, beneficiaries may choose between BS-VI-compliant vehicles and electric vehicles, allowing greater flexibility while ensuring substantial reductions in emissions.

This calibrated approach balances environmental priorities with operational realities across the NCR.

Seamless Digital Implementation

The scheme will be implemented through a dedicated online platform—the Parivahan PARIVARTAN Portal—(https://parivartan.parivahan.gov.in) providing an end-to-end digital experience for beneficiaries.

Through the portal, vehicle owners will be able to:

  • Check eligibility
  • Register their vehicles
  • Apply for incentives
  • Track application status
  • Access scheme-related information

The digital platform is designed to ensure transparency, efficiency and ease of access throughout the vehicle replacement process.

A Collaborative Effort

The PARIVARTAN Scheme is being implemented through coordinated efforts of the Central Government, State Governments, and the automobile industry. Participating States will provide up to 100 per cent Motor Vehicle Tax concession for ten years and full waiver of registration fees for eligible beneficiaries.

To facilitate effective implementation of the PARIVARTAN Scheme, the Ministry of Road Transport and Highways (MoRTH) has signed MoUs with 11 leading Original Equipment Manufacturers (OEMs)—Ashok Leyland, Switch Mobility, Tata Motors, Mahindra & Mahindra, SML Mahindra, Daimler India Commercial Vehicles (DICV), Eicher Trucks and Buses (VECV), Force Motors, Pinnacle Mobility Solutions, Olectra Greentech Limited, and Montra Electric (TI Clean Mobility Private Limited). Together, these OEMs account for over 95 per cent of India’s domestic truck and bus market, ensuring wider availability of eligible cleaner vehicles.

The scheme will be overseen by an Empowered Committee chaired by the Cabinet Secretary, comprising the CEO, NITI Aayog; Secretaries of MoHUA, MoRTH, MoPNG, and DFS; Chief Secretaries of Delhi-NCR States; and Member Secretary, NCRPB as Member Convenor. At the district level, District Collectors/District Magistrates will facilitate implementation and monitor progress.

Towards Cleaner Air and Sustainable Growth

The PARIVARTAN Scheme marks a significant milestone in the Government's efforts to build a cleaner, more sustainable and future-ready transport ecosystem. By promoting fleet modernisation and encouraging the adoption of cleaner technologies, the initiative is expected to contribute to improved air quality and support India's long-term environmental and sustainable development goals.

***
